title: LOVE this game - great graphics, fascinating to play
text:
My husband and I bought a Wii on a whim after Thanksgiving and 7 different games to get us started. We bought games in a variety of genres so we could get a real feel for the system & figure out what we really enjoy. After trying a couple of other shooting games with the Wii pistol attachment for the Wii Remotes, "Dead Space Extraction" is the winner! This game is by far the best of all the games we've tried, including those that are not in the shooting categories.

The graphics are amazing, the story line was quick-paced, made sense and the story actually had us wanting to know more. We loved being able to play side by side on a single screen without having to do the whole split screen effect - each of us has our own cross-hairs to aim and shoot the aliens with, but on one screen so we can make full use of the 50" television. The other nice thing about this game was that the main characters change without losing the flow of the story and the point of the game - keeps things interesting and stirs up the skill set. There are multiple difficulty levels here as well so when you think you've mastered it, you can come back and let it kick your butt all over again. SO GLAD WE BOUGHT THIS ONE!

title: Not the best Atelier game, unfortunately :/
text:
I'm such a fan of Atelier! But this one is the game I like the least. The story is fun and enjoyable, and the characters are pretty neat. That said, there are several annoying things with the game. For starters, if you leave your home and go to the shop to sell an over-abundance of items, you have to have the items in your basket. So that means making SEVERAL trips between your home and shops. That might not sound so bad to you, but you have no idea... if you forget to sell your needless items, your inventory will cap out, and you'll be forced to pick and choose, then run back and forth selling. It's so tedious, and I swear I can feel myself getting older during it.

This IS a good game, though!

title: I got what I expected, and honestly enjoyed it.
text:
Chulip, from its pictures alone, is obviously a game with bad graphics. However, I'm not one to judge a game on its graphics alone. I liked the idea of a 'kissing RPG', and wanted to try it out!

Voices: My god, what in the hell are they saying? They didn't bother re-dubbing voices. They repeat the same lines over and over, which won't make sense to you at all, while text appears on the bottom of the screen. This was a small annoyance that I quickly got used to.

What I loved was the challenge of gaining all those kisses. For everyone's information: ALL available kisses in the game are listed in the manual that come WITH the game, and even explains how to gain them. There's no need to buy or look up a guide.

I felt a sense of triumph when I gained all kisses! It wasn't easy, and I did have a LOT of fun. This game is cheap used, and I highly recommended it for someone looking for an inexpensive challenge.

title: What a great series!!
text:
I love to play games of all kinds, but many of the DS games are just not my style.
(I am one of the few people around that don't really care for Mario, I suppose! Jumping
for coins or mushrooms just isn't my thing.)

This game is absolutely crammed with brain teasers. Nothing that would take a PhD to solve, and
they vary in difficulty from easy to super hard. The difficulty is rated in "picarats", the point system
the game uses.

Like other Layton games, there is a mystery to solve. However, this one had a lot more to do than the
Curious Village game. There are extra games in Layton's "trunk", and you have to find ingredients to brew
various teas. In the course of the game you will come across characters that are thirsty and really want a nice
cuppa tea of some sort. It will be your job to brew what they want. If you serve the right one, it will unlock
yet another puzzle.

I finished Curious Village completely in about 16 hours of play time. (I wasn't rushing, but still wasn't all that
hard.) So far, I have been playing for about 22 hours, and still not completed. This is just more fun. You can keep
going back to places you've already been to, and there will be another puzzle.

There is also a place to collect pieces of a camera that was "dropped". Once you reassemble the camera, there are
several places where you can take a "photo". That is yet another part of the game - you then compare the real scene
with the photo you took, and spot three differences. If you get them all (per photo and there are 12), it unlocks yet
another puzzle.

I really truly love this series, and hope they continue to make them every year.
I can hardly wait for the next two. These are a little pricey, but honestly, they are worth it.
Lots of fun game play. All the puzzles are woven into a storyline that involves a lot of characters to solve
the mystery.

If you like brain teasers or even puzzles like Hi-Q, get this game. You won't be sorry.

title: I really like this controller - it feels good in your hands.
text:
I am not the video game expert in our house, but I have it on good authority that
these are great! This is the second one of the iGlow controllers we have purchased.
The first one was the black iGlow.

Note that for some reason, the iGlow controllers come packaged in a box that uses
magnets as the closure. Just a heads-up so you do not put the boxes near items in your
room that might be sensitive to magnetic fields, such as computers or possibly stereos.
No clue why they did not use Velcro, but I guess someone gave them a great deal on magnets!

Both controllers use blue LED lighting to create a nice visual effect while playing.
It makes playing games in a dark room a lot better!

I've included a photo of both the white and the black together so you can see the
differences. It looks to me like the same basic light, but the black vs white crackle effect
gives a very different look to it all.

They have a great feel to them, and the lights just make it all better.
We use them with a Playstation 2. So far, we have not experienced any lag or other
problems with the game play.

I saw that a lot of the other reviews said this model broke easily.
We have not experienced that, but we don't have little children - ours are older.
Perhaps it is the care of the controller that makes it last better?
We haven't had anything break in the time we've been using it. We've had ours since
December 2010 without any problems. We don't toss it in a drawer though - we have a
plastic storage bin that the controllers go in to. I could see it being easy to break
if it was tossed onto something hard. Other than that - ours is going strong.

All in all, highly recommended!

title: Fun little game, even for us "older folks" ...
text:
I'm relatively new to the Nintendo DS Lite (and video-based games in general), having just received the unit at Christmas, but I'm getting a lot of enjoyment out of it.

As a kid, I always loved the "find the object in the picture" puzzles in various children's magazines. Nothing has changed much! As a much older adult (ahem!), I still get a kick out of scrutinizing a picture to try to find various "hidden" objects. This particular game would probably would be suitable for someone 10 yrs old and up. Some of the clues may need explanation for younger kids ("ocean predator," "Roman 10," etc.).

The artwork in this game is very nice. And I really like the fact that, from the very beginning, you're tasked with finding tiny relatively obscure objects as well as larger more obvious ones.

As you progress through the levels, the number of objects increases (as does the time to find them, to a point). But part of the task might be finding multiple occurrences of an "object" -- say, "3 bats" or "2 spider homes." And those bats? well, how many definitions are there for "bat"? Just be prepared to broaden your search to more than just *one* type of item. So, if you need to find 36 "objects," you may actually need to locate closer to 45 or so, depending on the number of multiples you're asked to locate. This makes it more interesting, in my view. As you finish a level, you're offered another kind of puzzle to solve: word search, jigsaw puzzle, mah johng, tile rotate -- none of which are very difficult.

The story? Well, basically, there's a narrative/text story that sort of runs along in the background, but seems to have little to do with the objects you're asked to find. Your "locations" are all in the town where the alleged art theft occurred, but beyond that, they play little role in your activities, other than to serve as the backdrops for your seek-and-find activities. At no time are you asked to try to solve the crime -- in fact, the culprit and plot are all laid out for you, seemingly disjointed from the puzzles. You simply solve the puzzles. That's it. Eventually, you finish by getting through all the levels and finding the items you're asked to find.

Still, it's a beautifully rendered game, and I'll probably play it again.

Fun little game, even for us "older folks" ... I'm relatively new to the Nintendo DS Lite (and video-based games in general), having just received the unit at Christmas, but I'm getting a lot of enjoyment out of it.

As a kid, I always loved the "find the object in the picture" puzzles in various children's magazines. Nothing has changed much! As a much older adult (ahem!), I still get a kick out of scrutinizing a picture to try to find various "hidden" objects. This particular game would probably would be suitable for someone 10 yrs old and up. Some of the clues may need explanation for younger kids ("ocean predator," "Roman 10," etc.).

The artwork in this game is very nice. And I really like the fact that, from the very beginning, you're tasked with finding tiny relatively obscure objects as well as larger more obvious ones.

As you progress through the levels, the number of objects increases (as does the time to find them, to a point). But part of the task might be finding multiple occurrences of an "object" -- say, "3 bats" or "2 spider homes." And those bats? well, how many definitions are there for "bat"? Just be prepared to broaden your search to more than just *one* type of item. So, if you need to find 36 "objects," you may actually need to locate closer to 45 or so, depending on the number of multiples you're asked to locate. This makes it more interesting, in my view. As you finish a level, you're offered another kind of puzzle to solve: word search, jigsaw puzzle, mah johng, tile rotate -- none of which are very difficult.

The story? Well, basically, there's a narrative/text story that sort of runs along in the background, but seems to have little to do with the objects you're asked to find. Your "locations" are all in the town where the alleged art theft occurred, but beyond that, they play little role in your activities, other than to serve as the backdrops for your seek-and-find activities. At no time are you asked to try to solve the crime -- in fact, the culprit and plot are all laid out for you, seemingly disjointed from the puzzles. You simply solve the puzzles. That's it. Eventually, you finish by getting through all the levels and finding the items you're asked to find.

Still, it's a beautifully rendered game, and I'll probably play it again.

The only other game like this I have is "Mystery Case Files: MillionHeir" -- they're very similar, but I probably like "Mystery P.I.: Portrait of a Thief" a little better, mostly due to the art and the variety of the other puzzles.

title: Not what it promises to be.
text:
This is a game that had a TON of potential, but completely missed the mark.

I was extremely excited for all that this game promise.. This game promises No Classes, No Levels, Total Freedom of Play...the reality of the game is quite different.

I think everyone understood there was some wiggle room in their marketing statements, as there would be some type of progression and "leveling", which there is. Instead of the traditional leveling, you earn Skill Points and Ability points and apply them to a "skill wheel", which unlocks different skills for different weapons. This ultimately allows for a single character to take on any role in the game.. wanna be a tank, switch weapons, wanna be a healer, switch weapons, so the only real reason to create an "alt" is to join a different faction or for cosmetic purposes.

Unfortunately, where the game goes horribly wrong is in the forced progression curve, which winds up being far more restrictive and linear than many of the other MMORPG's I played (including SWTOR, which had a very linear and specific storyline to follow).

The usual MMO experience is you move into a zone, pick up all the quests, do the quests, gain experience "clear" the zone and then move onto the next, harder zone. Some people choose to focus on one quest at a time, some people follow a specific storyline, and some people grab everything in place and grind through quests as fast as possible... Secret World is NO DIFFERENT in set up. If you do not clear most of the zone, you will not be powerful enough to move onto the next zone. However, unlike other MMO's, Secret World restricts HOW you go through the zone and forces you to constantly backtrack in a forced time sink.

In The Secret World, you accept mission A from character A. On the way to your objective you encounter character B who requests you also to complete a task at the same place. You go to accept this new missions thinking "cool, I can kill two birds with one stone" and you get a warning window that you must "pause" quest A to accept quest B. If you choose to pause quest A and take quest B, you have to go back to character A to "unpause" quest A, leaving you to run back and forth over the same ground several times... and it isn't just character A and B, you come across character C, D, E, F and G along the way and each time you talk to them you are told you can't accept their missions without abandoning the mission you are on... Freedom of play? Why can't I get BOTH bandages and medication from the pharmacy at the same time?? No, I have to get the bandages, return them to character A, then find character D again, go back to the same pharmacy and find the medication and return it to character D and then hunt out character B who wanted water from the store which was right next to the pharmacy.

The developers have offered several conflicting excuses for this baffling limitation, everything from "memory problems on the backend" to it being a high level decision made to force you to get immersed in each mission, instead of treating characters like mission hubs. Ultimately, one honest dev admitted that if they removed the limitation it would break the progression curve and they would have to reduce the amount of experience you gained from each mission and people would complain there isn't enough content. (ie, we need to force you to run back and forth because you would progress through the game too fast if we allowed you to follow a logical progression.)

This brings me back to the main selling point... "TOTAL FREEDOM OF PLAY" If I am someone who chooses to grind quests, why is there something wrong with that? If am someone who WANTS to focus on one quest at a time, great. If I want to do 3 at a time, why am I not allowed to make that choice? They made it 100% clear in the forums that this system was NOT up for debate and would NOT be changed under any circumstances. This non-intuitive questing system made the game feel like work, rather than fun. I was looking for a game that offered more freedom of gameplay and this felt exactly the opposite.

title: A great start with lots of potential - Potential failed... Cancelled my sub.
text:
Leaving my previous review below, because it was written before patch 1.2 and what this game was to become, so you can read my original optimism!

What ruined potential. Once you hit level 50, the game becomes an absolute mindless grind, with no sense of purpose at all. It is one thing to do the same raids over and over if they are fun or have purpose, but it loses its luster quickly and becomes the usual (stand on the x, hit the 3 key seven times, then the 5 key times and then stand on spot Y). The PvP (basically now reduced to warzones ONLY) have absolutely no sense of purpose, except to grind for gear. They are supposedly introducing "team" play, but they missed the opportunity to have a overall purpose to the PvP, such as helping your chosen FACTION. Open world PvP is non-existent and had no sense of purpose either.

For a game that started off telling an amazing story... it completely loses its way towards the end and you just don't care about what happens anymore.

Space combat.. great potential gone wrong. You wind up repeating the exact same space missions during your initial progressions. (The level 40 missions are the exact same as the level 20 missions, just with slightly higher goals (kill 40 fighters instead of 20).

When they added content to the story in patch 1.2.. I didn't both to complete it as I had stopped caring about the storyline.

It's a shame, because this could have been a fantastic game, but they took the easy way out and decided to turn it into a mindless grind.

This is defiantly one of the better MMO's and has some aspects that make it much better than the rest.

The Best Aspects:

The story line is fantastic and the voice acting makes it much more enthralling than other games which simply present you with a wall of text. It maintains the feel of both an MMO and single player game.

Crafting. Finally a game got this right. You don't have to spend endless boring hours grinding away at resource gathering and standing over a forge. You get companions in the game and send them on missions and they gather the resources for you and craft the items, earning you experience. This is the first MMO where I am actually doing the crafting.

They have nice bonus systems to encourage you to group, but you don't HAVE TO if you don't want to in order to complete your story line. (If you group with others you earn experience from them completing quests as well as you own, so you level much faster!)

The Good Aspects:

Space combat is a lot of fun, but isn't fleshed out yet. You can do space missions, but are essentially stuck on a rail as your ship steers itself through space and you control where and what you shoot, with small room for movements.

Characters are pretty customizable, as you can switch your skill tree. So you can go up the healing tree and then decide you want to do DPS and go back to your trainer and spend some credits to reassign your skills. (You get the first swap for free). You can also create interesting hybrid characters, who can serve dual purposes.

What needs work:

The PVP just isn't there yet. There isn't anything to encourage people into open world PvP, so it is pretty much restricted to "warzones". These are mini, repeatable instances where they put equal number of republic and empire and give them a goal to achieve. Great idea.. execution isn't there yet. There is no in game voice communication, so you get thrown into a random group and then it becomes difficult to execute because you can't communicate quickly. Further they put people of all levels into the same warzone and although they scale your HP up to level 50, unless you are level 50, your gear and skills aren't on par. (Hopefully they will bracket the warzones in the future to make them more balanced).

Overall, however, this is a great game that has lots of potential. Hopefully they resist the urge to go with other MMO's have gone before them and just turn it into a constant grind for gear. Right now, it isn't grindy and that alone makes it worth playing!

title: Doesn't live up to its expectations...
text:
I am a huge fan of Roberta Williams, her King's Quest games have offered me hours of entertainment since I was about 9 years old. When I heard that she was taking on a more "adult" project featuring real actors and a gripping, horror-based storyline, I was more than excited. However, I received nothing but disappointment.
The graphics in this game are most impressive (considering the time that the game was created). They feature real actors who are placed in front of a blue screen with a cartoon-ish backround and props projected behind them. This gives the game a fairly realistic effect although at times the actors look so out of place in front of their backrounds that the occuring event is everything but real.
As far as the acting goes..it's about what you'd expect from a game which resembles a B horror movie. Most of the acting is barely believeable (although Adrienne, the main character, is not horrible) and the characters themselves are most annoying.
The story was just awful...cliched and robbed to the core, I found absolutely everything in this game to be entirely predictable. It focuses around a couple, Don and Adrienne, who move into a huge, spooky house on an island. The house was owned by a creepy count named Carno and it is said to be haunted. All of the islanders are afraid of the house and none of them are too keen on talking about it (with the exception of one eager old woman who serves as the "revelation of the evil within" source seen in all movies of this sort). The story proceeds just as you would predict. Without giving anything away I'll just tell you that Adrienne discovers ghosts, secret rooms, and a demon which has been wreaking havoc on the house for years. It borrows heavily from Stephen King's "The Shining" (as in..the house turns the husband into a raving psychopath). For anyone who is not too familiar with the horror genre, Phantasmagoria may provide a few hours of good story. To fans of classic horror movies and games, Phantasmagoria will become stale before the end of chapter three.
This brings me to the gameplay. The game itself is divided into 7 chapters (each chapter contained entirely on its respective disk). While this may seem as though it allows for a massive game, it must be said that each chapter can be completed in a quick half hour, even by the most inexperienced of adventure gamers. The puzzles that each chapter requires you to solve are completely lacking in challenge. They are solved by the use of obvious items in Adrienne's inventory and no logical thought is necessary. There was actually a chapter in the game which focused entirely on buying a bottle of Dran-O from the village general store and returning it to your husband. Yes - that's it. Later - a puzzle comes up where the very item you need can be found a single screen below and it is not hidden in the very least.
To fans of blood and gore - this game may serve as an enjoyable "shockfest". There is more than one moment of senseless violence which is not limited to beheading, faces being ripped open, and the funneling of human body parts down a woman's throat. For those too squeamish to even imagine such things, the gore can easily be censored with an in-game option requiring the entry of a password (to protect the little ones' virgin eyes).
Overall, Phantasmagoria lacks in every area required to make an adventure game reach "classic" status. The story is predictable, the gameplay simple and stale, and the characters annoying. For huge fans of senseless violence and B-movie horror plots, this may serve as some sort of "cult classic" piece. All others, don't waste your money.

As far as the acting goes..it's about what you'd expect from a game which resembles a B horror movie. Most of the acting is barely believeable (although Adrienne, the main character, is not horrible) and the characters themselves are most annoying.
The story was just awful...cliched and robbed to the core, I found absolutely everything in this game to be entirely predictable. It focuses around a couple, Don and Adrienne, who move into a huge, spooky house on an island. The house was owned by a creepy count named Carno and it is said to be haunted. All of the islanders are afraid of the house and none of them are too keen on talking about it (with the exception of one eager old woman who serves as the "revelation of the evil within" source seen in all movies of this sort). The story proceeds just as you would predict. Without giving anything away I'll just tell you that Adrienne discovers ghosts, secret rooms, and a demon which has been wreaking havoc on the house for years. It borrows heavily from Stephen King's "The Shining" (as in..the house turns the husband into a raving psychopath). For anyone who is not too familiar with the horror genre, Phantasmagoria may provide a few hours of good story. To fans of classic horror movies and games, Phantasmagoria will become stale before the end of chapter three.
This brings me to the gameplay. The game itself is divided into 7 chapters (each chapter contained entirely on its respective disk). While this may seem as though it allows for a massive game, it must be said that each chapter can be completed in a quick half hour, even by the most inexperienced of adventure gamers. The puzzles that each chapter requires you to solve are completely lacking in challenge. They are solved by the use of obvious items in Adrienne's inventory and no logical thought is necessary. There was actually a chapter in the game which focused entirely on buying a bottle of Dran-O from the village general store and returning it to your husband. Yes - that's it. Later - a puzzle comes up where the very item you need can be found a single screen below and it is not hidden in the very least.
To fans of blood and gore - this game may serve as an enjoyable "shockfest". There is more than one moment of senseless violence which is not limited to beheading, faces being ripped open, and the funneling of human body parts down a woman's throat. For those too squeamish to even imagine such things, the gore can easily be censored with an in-game option requiring the entry of a password (to protect the little ones' virgin eyes).
Overall, Phantasmagoria lacks in every area required to make an adventure game reach "classic" status. The story is predictable, the gameplay simple and stale, and the characters annoying. For huge fans of senseless violence and B-movie horror plots, this may serve as some sort of "cult classic" piece. All others, don't waste your money.

title: Impressive
text:
"Wow," is the best I can think of to say about this game. It's really something and I like it a lot. Usually I only play serious strategy games such as Civilization and my past forays into console games have been far less than satisfactory. Thanks to the other reviewers here I decided to give this one a try and I'm very glad I did.

At first I was wondering if it is just an interactive story. I'm not much for the story aspects of games and it took several scenes before actual game play comes up. Surprisingly, I held in there and after the first couple short missions I was hooked. The story itself is not overly original but also not so common as to be boring. The main characters are likeable enough and as things progressed I found myself interested in what was going on and anxious to find out what would happen next.

So then, the Pros: The Graphics, great! I wasn't sure what to think of the watercolor/cartoon/anime mix at first but after seeing it in action I'm hooked. While most modern games seem to be going for the "real as life" look this game looks softer, less in your face. Also on the plus side of things is the ease of play. It was easy to learn how things work and to understand the goals and objectives set out. I got an Xbox controller to use with it, my first time ever using one, and I'm having a great time with it.

Another plus, to me, is the music. I often turn the music or all sound off when playing games because I usually find it distracting or somehow undesirable. This one is different and interesting is that parts of the music, while certainly different, is reminiscent of songs I've heard, some old and some not so old.

On the Cons side of things I'm coming up a little short. I would prefer to not have go through a configuration launcher every time and sometimes the story plays on emotions in ways I'd rather it didn't. Sometimes the story scenes are a bit long and I would get impatient for the next mission. And of course there's always those times such as when my best gunner totally misses the house sized tank 20 feet in from of him and gets me ranting and wanting an undo/redo/wtf button. But that's part of luck and chance and it wouldn't be a real game without. None of these things warrant losing even one star so my rating stands at 5 out of 5.

All in all I think this is one of the most refined and polished games I've ever played. It's done. Totally complete and playable on initial download. No waiting weeks or months for patches and updates. No hours spent grinding through forums hoping to find a fix for some inane problem. This game works and works well.

When the next episode or book in the story is released for the PC I will most certainly buy it too.

5 out of 5 stars for this one and kudos for the developers. Well Done!

title: Overpriced and Uninspired
text:
I had really hoped for more from this game. Sadly it's more or less Civ 5 in new clothes with most of Civ 5's best features lost in the translation. Same as many others I've waited years for them to "finish" civ 5 and thought this would be a good culmination of their work. Wrong! This is more like starting over with a big step backwards.

I regret giving them my 50 bucks for this, it should have been downloadable content for civ 5. At least then some of the polish they'd achieved would have been carried over.

UPDATE: Minus another star, was 3 now 2. I've played several games of this new civ so far, they go much faster than usual. There are some neat things and now that I've got used to the interface it's ok too. What isn't ok is having to play on only random maps. No scenarios, no meticulously setting up the perfect game. And I'm sorry to say, random gets boring and repetitive very fast.

Hopefully soon they will release a map and scenario editor and given things like that have, for a very long time, been a part of Sid Meier's Civilization, it's pretty lame they release this game without it. IMHO.

2nd UPDATE: It's been a month now and still no update so there goes another star.

On a positive note, the game does play nicely. It moves along with an ease I've not before noticed in any civ and the soft sounds for events don't make me cringe.

title: Great Keyboard -  Great Price
text:
First off I want to note that I got this when it was priced at $29.99, perhaps the best deal I've ever got on a keyboard. I replaced a CM Storm Trigger with this after the Storm developed connection issues after only 3 months, probably the worst deal I've ever got on a keyboard.

I wish I had bought this one first because I like it better than the cm storm. It's much lighter and much, much easier to program. Obviously it doesn't have the nice cherry switches like the storm does and I am concerned on how long it will last, but it's a great keyboard and the touch is fine, I can't complain.

At first I was worried about the green lighting, I thought it would look strange and be hard to see. To my surprise it looks great and is very easy to see. To my eyes I'd have to say it's easier to see than either red or blue light, both of which I've had before.

And because I do all my typing with the keyboard resting between my indian style crossed legs it's light weight is great, so much better than having 3 pounds of keyboard digging into my legs.

The only CON I've found is sometimes when I type the keys will squeak a little and that is a bit annoying. If it ever gets bad I'll just pull the caps and touch the springs up with a bit of oil.

My only regret is that I didn't buy 2 or 3 of them when they were priced so low.

text: I bought the K55 from corsair because my wife was tired of hearing the constant click click click fromy my razar keyboard. Plus the FN+(number) to change the lighting doesn't work at all once booted into windows. I thought for awhile I had figured it out but the first time I launched a game the leds turned off. Okay that was interesting. I tried 3 other games. Each they'd load, lights off. Exit to the desktop the lights would come back on. Well guess what. I need to see my keyboard when gaming. Nothing in the documentation or support forums I've found has said anything about this. Anyway this is my first purchase of a Corsair product and based on this alone they won't be my first choice in the future.

Units need to deal more damage, as battles drag out much longer than they should.

the cord's really good (I was worried about the nylon cording but so far no trouble)

text:

If you're offended by violence, cursing, or a complete disregard for offending anyone than I'd suggest you steer clear of this title. For the rest of you, grab a copy and immerse yourself in hilarity. There's no attempt at making them look 'real' or make the graphics more dramatic. It's the simplicity of this game that makes this game fun.

Admittedly I do allow my son (now 17) to play games such as Halo, Left for Dead an Skyrim so the rating didn't faze me. I said, "yeah, but it looks like it would be fun" and to his surprise, it is... one of his favorite parts so far is right at the beginning when you select your player name. It had us all laughing hysterically and he keeps bringing it up in conversation.

title: love these headphones, but...
text:
When I got these headphones I thought it would be a great way to avoid having to listen to whatever gaming system my son was playing on the television. Unfortunately do they not only drown out his yelling at the TV, but they also don't quiet the gaming noise either (I thought all you had to do was plug the device into the proper slot on the HD TV and instant silence, not so). Instead, my husband and son sat there for an hour going through the various ways to turn off the sound on the television and finally found some button on the remote that mutes it. However, if they forget to undo it when they're done then I'm stuck with a mute television and no clue how to fix it. LOL I don't know how it would work with any other kind of TV. We have a Vizio (if anybody has figured out how to get the headphones to work without all the drama please let me know!)

Now, that being said, the headphones work beautifully for the computer, iPad, and iPhone and the sound is awesome. I really love how big the earcovers are as well. I wear glasses so my ear isn't being pressed down onto the frame (which hurts after awhile). The glow from the headset is very cool even though you can't see it when you're wearing them but still... it makes a useful device neat to look at :) The headphones are on the large size so any visions I had of packing them to the local library for a few hours of mindless internet usage using them is out (the black piece you see in the picture sits on the top of your head - everything above that is actually way above it if that gives you any idea of how large these are.

When I asked my son if he had anything to add, he said the microphone could be a little longer. Apparently it only extends to the side of his face and he'd prefer it be closer to his mouth. Otherwise he loves this headset. It makes it much easier for him to sneak internet gaming time.

text:
we're more than a little ticked off at the way it's presented! If you don't have high speed internet don't bother buying the collector's edition because the extra costumes have to be downloaded from online. For the price we paid they should have had the costumes on a separate disc or even had the game disk already contain the costumes. At the very least there should be another option for us poor shmucks who live in the middle of nowhere and don't have an option of high speed internet.

title: Great in some ways, not so in others
text:
Ok first off, I had the Rift before this S model, so this is somewhat of a comparison.

The Rift S is definitely more comfortable than it's predecessor. The foam is soft and it seems a tad lighter. I wear glasses, and the S does not rest on them as much as the last generation, which is good. I can spend much more time using the Rift S because it's comfort is that much better. The S also slips on and off my face a lot easier than the last generation and I have a large head, being 6'5" @ 275lbs.

It is great that it does not use external sensors to track movement, because it is just far less cumbersome and more of a simple plug and play device now. I have an Acer Predator 17, which has a display port, but the Rift S does come with an adapter if yours does not.

The controllers are the same size and weight, which is really good. They are far less bulky than it's competitors, which makes using the VR much more enjoyable in my opinion.

Headset tracking of itself is flawless, it is right on when you move your head around. However, I do get headset out of bounds type messages just looking around sometimes and that is annoying.

Eye relief, I don't really know about. I've adjusted it to max (72) and least and noticed zero difference in anything.

The bad news.

External tracking of the controllers is glitchy and glitchy a lot. You no longer have a fine tracking experience that is so smooth, as it was in the previous Rift. Your hands in the VR like to twitch, jump and sometimes freeze. It's not 100% of the time that it does this, but it happens frequently enough to be bothersome. The rest of the time it is smooth and responsive.

Optics. This is where the Rift S falls even shorter, in my experience. For starters, your field of view has reduced and it is not quite as immersive as the previous Rift. For example, it is as though you are looking through toilet paper tubes now, as there are large black areas of nothing surrounding the visual field. Tunnel vision. Although the experience is still fun, I am very disappointed in this, as it has lost some of it's VR experience as a result.

The resolution is supposed to be higher, but I do not see that at all. Fonts are still grainy and it is too similar to the last Rift to say that there is much, if any improvement in resolution.

The screen brightness is less in the Rift S, so it loses points for that. Although still pretty vibrant, it's just lacking something I can't exactly put my finger on.

Overall, it is a step back from the Rift in the critical areas a VR should be and a step forward in comfort and convenience. It all depends on what is more important to you.

I wear glasses, and the S does not rest on them as much as the last generation, which is good. I can spend much more time using the Rift S because it's comfort is that much better. The S also slips on and off my face a lot easier than the last generation and I have a large head, being 6'5" 275lbs. It is great that it does not use external sensors to track movement, because it is just far less cumbersome and more of a simple plug and play device now. I have an Acer Predator 17, which has a display port, but the Rift S does come with an adapter if yours does not. The controllers are the same size and weight, which is really good. They are far less bulky than it's competitors, which makes using the VR much more enjoyable in my opinion. Headset tracking of itself is flawless, it is right on when you move your head around. However, I do get headset out of bounds type messages just looking around sometimes and that is annoying. Eye relief, I don't really know about. I've adjusted it to max 72 and least and noticed zero difference in anything. The bad news. External tracking of the controllers is glitchy and glitchy a lot. You no longer have a fine tracking experience that is so smooth, as it was in the previous Rift. Your hands in the VR like to twitch, jump and sometimes freeze. It's not 100 of the time that it does this, but it happens frequently enough to be bothersome. The rest of the time it is smooth and responsive. Optics. This is where the Rift S falls even shorter, in my experience. For starters, your field of view has reduced and it is not quite as immersive as the previous Rift. For example, it is as though you are looking through toilet paper tubes now, as there are large black areas of nothing surrounding the visual field. Tunnel vision. Although the experience is still fun, I am very disappointed in this, as it has lost some of it's VR experience as a result. The resolution is supposed to be higher, but I do not see that at all. Fonts are still grainy and it is too similar to the last Rift to say that there is much, if any improvement in resolution. The screen brightness is less in the Rift S, so it loses points for that. Although still pretty vibrant, it's just lacking something I can't exactly put my finger on. Overall, it is a step back from the Rift in the critical areas a VR should be and a step forward in comfort and convenience. It all depends on what is more important to you.

title: GTA 4 Where have you been all my life!
text:
I have never played or even knew about the GTA series until yesterday! What an awesome game! I purchased the digital download because I could not wait to go buy the CD at a store. The YouTube videos cracked me up!

The 13 gig download took about 2 hours on my 20 meg cable connection. After it self extracted, it launched the installer. Installation was a breeze and went off without a hook. I launched the game and Games for Windows Live automatically updated and patched it without any issues. The graphics were nice on default but I wanted to set everything to max. Went to options and maxed out the video settings (GeForce GTX 580). When I clicked apply, the game kicked me to the desktop and then I got worried because of all the negative reviews on Amazon.

Since I am running Windows 7 64 bit edition, I went in and set the game to run as administrator. It started flawlessly and to my surprise, had applied and saved my video settings. I started a new game and it has performed remarkably and without error or flaw! I am getting excellent frame rates and not so much as a hiccup.

I have nothing but high praise for this game and I am very glad I got it!

Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-2600K CPU @ 3.40GHz (8 CPUs), ~3.4GHz

Viper 12288MB RAM

GeForce GTX 580

title: A Little Known Gem of a Game
text: I really liked this game. I had never heard of it before, until I did an impromptu search for games by Ubisoft and found it in the list. A quick view of what the game was like on YouTube and I decided to try it. The story is interesting, and teases you all the way to the end. It has challenging puzzles and the gameplay mechanics are easy to master. I'm not a huge fan of 1st person style gameplay, but it worked well in this game and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Since you play as one type of character (mage, warrior, assassin, etc...) you can play the game more than once using a different skill set each time. You can also choose whether to be evil or good, which will change the story as well. If you like Oblivion, Dragon Age or The Witcher, I think you will really enjoy this game as well. There are multi-player online options of play as well, that will further extend your enjoyment of the game.

title: joy-cons fit a little too tightly and charging status indication could be better
text:
I purchased this product because I wanted a grip for my second set of joycons and while I was at it, I wanted an easy way to charge those controllers.

Whie this grip looks like it will do everything I need (it will charge the joycons while connected to the power adapter or on battery power and it provides a satin grip that keep the controllers secure), execution could have been better.

Here are some of my complaints:
-- The grip has a satin surface which is somewhat outdated, I think. Most manufacturers mold textures into the plastic to give them grip. My past experience with satin surfaces is that after a few years, they become a sticky mess.
-- Perhaps it is the product that I got but I charged the grip overnight without the joycons inserted and the red charging light was still on when I checked on it in the morning so there is no indication that the charging has completed. This might mean that there is no cut-off for when the battery is fully charged.
-- The joy-cons fit too snugly. It is actually a little difficult to slide the controllers in and out of the grip. This could be because of the satin finish that is sprayed on to the underlying plastic.

Other features:
-- Charges the joycons with the built-in battery pack. A blue light indicates that the controllers are charging.
-- Not much heavier than the original switch grip.
-- Wider than the original grip. For me, this is actually more comfortable.

Again, this will meet my requirements but I wonder how long the internal battery pack will last if there is no charging cut-off.

-- 7.1 surround - I've always see this more as a gimmick than an actual feature, even in headphones that cost hundreds of dollars but don't have discreet speakers. The computer sees these headsets as stereo and not 7.1 so whatever program you run, whether it's a trailer with Dolby Atmos or a game, the output will still be stereo. While their program supposedly tries to simulate virtual surround, you would still need the source to be 7.1 discreet channels so that their driver can process the signal to simulate surround sound. These headsets do not have DTS-HD or Dolby ATMOS certification so they aren't actually able to process raw 7.1 channel data. It means that in the end, the video player is still just playing stereo sound. The end effect of turning on virtual 7.1 surround sound is that the soundtrack is more "atmospheric" or "wider" sounding, but you wouldn't be able to tell that a sound is coming from your rear left flank. Since I never expected much out of this feature, I didn't mind that it wasn't true 7.1

-- USB - True plug and play on Windows 10. I plugged these headphones in and immediately, Windows output sound through them. No muss no fuss. It just worked. You can install their driver, which turns on the "virtual 7.1" feature but that's pretty much like installing drivers for any realtek sound card. You just have access to a few extra DSP effects. Honestly, I don't like extra processing to my audio signals. Being USB, it is a completely digital signal to your headphones all the way up until the speakers themselves. On 3.5mm headphones, the audio signal is analog at 3.5mm port, at which point, you will get some signal degradation just from the connection itself.

-- Gaming Headset with Microphone - I don't really play games online so I can't tell you whether the microphone is better or worse than any other headset but I can tell you that I used the Spirit Wolf with a few games and I was hearing sounds that I didn't hear in my Sennheisers.

-- PC Gamers - BONUS! This headset isn't just for PC gaming, it works with the Nintendo switch, too, using the USB port on the dock. Even the volume buttons on the headset works!

My overall experience with Spirit Wolf has been positive. The sound is crisp and clear and the high frequencies are very good but the bass could have been better. I'm not big on turning up the bass so it's not a big loss. I still feel that the overall sound quality is very good.

The headset is circumaural which means it surrounds your ears and the speakers are not pressed right against your head. It means that noise isolation isn't as good as earbuds or even supra-aural headphones (which press up against your ear), but there's a reason professional gaming headphones are this style. You can wear them for longer periods without discomfort and you are able to achieve a wider sound.

Overall, I recommend this headset for its price and overall sound quality. The ability to use it with my Switch is just bonus.

EDIT: I must amend my previous conclusions regarding the virtual surround sound. I recently started playing Shadow of the Tomb Raider and as a test, I went into the audio settings for the game. The options were stereo, 5.1, 7.1, and spatial sound. Reading the description for spatial sound, it states that it is meant to be used with Windows Spatial Sound (right click on the speaker icon in your system tray and you'll see an option to turn it on). Well, I tried the spatial sound in three different ways: with only the in-game spatial sound setting on, the in-game setting + Windows Spatial Sound on, and in-game setting + XEar driver 7.1 on. All three give slightly different positional sound effects but I found that the XEar effect was the best. The sounds simulate a wide environment and I was able to distinguish the direction of each distinct sound source. Very impressive.

title: Decent HARD case for travel - charging a bit of a trick when in case.
text:
Many Nintendo Switch cases have hit the market since the release of the versatile gaming system and this this one meets all of the critical criteria of a good case but falls a bit short in order to be considered great.

The Switch fits perfectly in the top with adequate padding to protect the critical top glass LED screen. The 2 Joy-Con controllers fit snugly into individual slots beneath the main unit and there is another secure area to store the power adapter (and a few games) which is a huge plus for this case - which many other cases neglect.

As I stated, for travel purposes, this case is excellent.

While this case advertises itself as one where you can “charge and play” - that is awkward at best. First the Joy-Cons do not comfortably fit on the primary unit while in the case. If too much pressure is applied to the screen while propped on the stand it moves too much for accurate game play.

I have to give this case 3 STARS - it will definitely protect your Nintendo Switch and all of its necessary accessories when traveling better than many other cases but it won’t be staying in the case as you play...

UPDATE TO ORIGINAL REVIEW: Now that my son has had more time using this case he has told me that he liked it much more than he initially did.

Since I do not actually use the Switch I had to write my review based on his impressions and as he has used it he has liked it more and more. Often when the Nintendo Switch is played in handheld mode the joycons are held separately from the central screen unit so the fact that they don’t fit on it in the case does not matter.

In his opinion this is the best case he has used for his Nintendo Switch and we would definitely recommend it as a great way to protect your investment.

title: comfortable to use and durable
text:
I really love this keyboard. I was actually surprised when I got the box how heavy and sturdy this product is. I do a lot of typing, and this is perfect for my needs. The keys are deep and have a nice, resounding click that lets you know whether or not you hit the key. The sound isn't intolerable, especially if there are other things going on in your environment. The battery life seems pretty good, even with the backlight being on the majority of the time. Overall, I'm really impressed with this product. I do, however, wish the manual that came with it was a bit more explanatory on the different functions, as I wasn't sure what all the terms meant and what difference the modes make in your typing experience. Otherwise, this is a great product for a price that does not seem unreasonable. I would recommend it to other people who type a lot and are looking for a reliable and comfortable experience.

title: fun and challenging
text:
I love all of the different farming games, but what i love about this one the most is the amount of animals you can eventually have if you keep working at it. Want 500 pigs? No problem. Want to focus on gardening instead? No worries. There is freedom to do what you want in this game, including being a goblin fighting miner.

There isn't anything gross or any graphic violence in this game, so it is good for kids and parents alike. There are some difficult to solve puzzles and sometimes finding the lost items in the game can be maddening, but really, overall, there is so much to do if you get stuck doing one thing, then you can easily move on to another.

This truly is a great game, although the graphics are a bit wonky, even though one expects that with these crafting games, it can make it hard on the eyes after a while.

text:

I like the photo abilities and the choice of vehicles, but honestly, I could have done without the planes and the boats. This game is a bit different and some of the races are too short, some of them are just silly IMO. The graphics are good for the most part and there is a lot to do, but sometimes the other players can be a real pain in the rear end and you can't always get away from them like you can in other games.

Overall, it's okay, but not what I was hoping for based on how great the first one was.

title: I finally understand what all the hype was about
text:
I've been a dedicated PlayStation user for many years, but I decided I wanted to see what X box was all about so I gave in and got one. I see now why people love it. I love just about everything about this game system--except that the remote require actual batteries and does not come as a standard rechargeable. That actually seems not only silly to me, but perhaps even prehistoric.

Otherwise, the games are great, and having the Game Pass and Live Gold is great too. I wanted to try those services out and now I can see that I really do want them. The X Box itself has some really great functionality, is easy to set up even for a technology numpty like me and I like the design and build of it. There are a great range of games available for the whole family, so as a parent, I like that as well.

I'm no longer sure that Playstation is it for me. We will see what happens in the future of gaming, but I have to say, I'm impressed with the X Box.

title: Lots of connection types, but annoying USB
text:
These are decent low end headphones. I'm not expecting high quality sound for the price, but they get the job done and have quite decent bass, although other tones could be a little clearer. But I have some issues with the connection type, which is the exact same experience I've had with other headsets in this price range: I like that these come with an option for both stereo and mic jacks (as 2 TRS 3.5mm plugs), or a combined TRRS with both mic and stereo in one (for phones, certain laptops, etc) via an adapter. But it also comes with a big annoying USB A cable which I can't get rid of. I understand the USB cable is for power which works the lights, etc, on this thing, but unlike the 2 cables which can be combined into one for smaller portable devices, the connection ports are just messy with a dangling USB cable if you don't need it.
In my personal opinion, there should be an option to detach the USB cable and/or have it plug into a null adapter on the TRS/TRRS adapter wire so it has somewhere to go. It just looks messy like this, and requires too many ports to look clean on a laptop even if you're using all of them. On a desktop this is less of an issue, however the logo still seems kind of cheesy on the side, so I guess I'm just not a fan of the aesthetics of this set. It DOES work however, so if all you want is the utility of it, it works alright. Personally, I'd go with either a fully digital USB model if you wanted that (nice clean single plug, no analog jacks), or one without the LED lights and therefore doesn't require the USB plug.

title: Works great for button based games and compatible with Motion Plus / Wii U
text: Syncs up and works great, unlike some third party Wii controllers this one even has the Motion Plus part built in (required for Wii U and specific games on the old Wii console).  Keep in mind, however, this *IS* a third party controller, so not everything is 100% to spec. For example, I noticed that when pointing to the screen, the hand cursor seems to move with somewhat more sensitivity than an authentic Nintendo Wii controller. This isn't that big of a deal, but if you are used to an authentic one, you might find you need to relearn your muscle memory movements when using this one. There is no difference for games that require button pressing (brawl, Donkey Kong, etc), which is actually what I bought it for (multiplayer games that don't require screen pointing). For me, its perfect, but minus one star for not being the same motion experience as Nintendo's.

title: Closest thing to being an actual Jedi.
text:
As a SW fan and a fan of Kinect games in general, this is just a hoot to play. My 8 year old son loved the demo on our 360, and begged me to buy it for us to play. I'll be honest, there are better Star Wars games out there. And there are even better Kinect games. But for the price this sells for used, if you've got a Kinect and even a slight affinity towards Jedi, this is a must have.
Some mini games are better than others- my son and I enjoy the Jedi adventure story, and I'll admit to playing Rancor Rampage to blow off some steam now and then. The Galactic Dance Off is kind of silly, though. Sort of makes it feel cheesy and cheap, (jar jar binks style, if you know what I mean), but I suppose they wanted it to be fun for everyone of all ages and interests, so kudos to the developers for doing exactly that!

If I may admit, when starting the Jedi adventure and being trained to use a light saber, I started to really get sucked into it. The Jedi Master instructed me on screen to reach for my light saber (which flew into my avatar's hand), and feel its weight as I swing it around. I did that, and for a moment I felt like "Aw yeah, I can feel it!". Tons of fun!

text:
Still playing through. The Clockwork Mansion mission has a Portal feel to it with the spaces behind walls and the disembodied voice that knows where you are which I think is neat. There's a "stats" menu that allows you to track the lethality of your playthrough so you're not angry at the end because rats ate that unconscious body you hid at the beginning of the level. The mechanics and feel of the game are on par with the original Dishonored. I feel like the guards are smarter. The new powers do not disappoint so far. I was worried guards would easily see me use far reach, but that hasn't been the case. I feel like there weren't a lot of issues with the original game, so this game just improves on it. The art, music, and story so far have definitely met my expectations. I love how it really puts the original in perspective and gives you a better idea of the empire.

My only issue is that after a few hours of play, my pause menu and save/load menus no longer have images, but have white boxes where the images would go. It hasn't affected game play though.

Love this game. I highly recommend it, especially if you liked the original.

title: An Amazing And Engrossing Story
text:
Trevor Noah is a comedian who now hosts the Daily Show. In this engrossing memoir, he writes poignantly about his childhood in South Africa. As the son of a black woman and white man, his birth was a crime since blacks and whites were separated with the strict apartheid laws and interracial marriages were strictly forbidden.

His mother, an unconventional, free spirit, chose to have him with a white man whom she did not love; she wanted a mixed race child.
Trevor’s Swedish father was not usually in the picture, although Trevor saw him in very rare circumstances. Trevor lived with his mother, but even going outside the house was dangerous. They would walk separately and pretend they were not together.

Trevor Noah did not fit easily into any race category. He was light-skinned and considered colored, although his culture was black. title: I can't believe this controller gets such high rating. I've never owned a single Xbox. An unbiased review.
text:
I can't believe this controller has 4.5 stars. The only thing I can think of is Sony fanboys inflating the reviews. Here's my honest review from a casual gamer who's had a Sega Master System, Sega Genesis, N64, Dreamcast, Wii, PS3, and PS4. I'm not loyal to any brand or company, so my view should be unbiased.

GOOD:
1. The small speaker on the controller isn't much, but I like it and think it adds something to gaming.
2. The headphone jack is also helpful.
3. The light bar is cool, not only for looks, but to identify the player.
4. Sticks are better than the PS3 sticks.
5. L2/R2 curve in (not as much as it should) which is a big improvement from PS3.
6. The grips are a nice texture which give you a good feeling of control.
7. Sticks are symmetrical (I prefer this).

BAD:
1. Quality/design issues. I've had two controllers break with a faulty R2 button. I was able to repair them myself via YouTube videos, but as a casual gamer, this shouldn't happen since I don't play all that much (2 - 5 hours per week).
2. A big one....battery life sucks. The battery life is about half of my older PS3 controllers (even with the light bar dimmed all the way). I'm always having to charge or worry about if my buddy's controller will fire up since it might have been sitting awhile.
3. Quality/design issues 2: I just noticed the rubber splitting on one of my controller (the one I use the least!). This is unacceptable.
4. Not a big one, but annoying....the option and share buttons are too small and should be more triangular and follow the curve of the circle the face buttons are on (hope that made sense). And I have very small hands for a man.
5. The grips (though well textured) are just round cylinders and don't feel like they mold to your hand. It's not terrible, but could be much much better.
6. Touchpad. Love the idea, however it seems like it's barely used, which means that real estate could have been better used for a one color LCD screen or something else.

That's it! The controller gets the job done, but for how much crap people give the DS3, this DS4 improves upon the DS3 in some areas, and fails miserably at others.

title: I know I'm in the minority, but this game is bad.
text:
I had MVC3 and traded it in and waited for UMVC3 and I completely wasted my time and money. Hard core fighting gamers will probably love this game, but I consider myself a casual to moderate fighting gamer. Here's the pros and cons:

Pros:
-Graphics are pretty cool and stylistic
-Characters are varied
-Marvel superheroes are always cool!

Cons:
-Online mode is supposed to match you up with people your own skill, however I'm noticing many "beginners" and "rookies" are kicking my butt. Then I realized that they aren't really rookies, but people either resesting their stats or creating separate accounts and starting over to easily beat people. That's why everyone I sometimes face user names like "taj134dod"
-The endings are super lame and a huge disappointment.
-Galactus seems a lot harder on this version than in MVC3 on normal.
-Air combos. Worse thing every to happen to fighting games. EVER. Back in the day, Street Fighter II styles, it was about timing and guessing your opponents moves. Now, it's about landing that initial strike (which is good), but then being rewarded for it by doing almost unlimited air combos and taking all of your opponents energy for one initial hit. One opponent used Magento and took almost all my life with one consistant air combo. Go back to a thinking man's fighting game and not fast fingers and NO EXPLOITS. Knocking an opponent into the air and then slamming them back to the ground is fine, but this is just ridiculous.
-You can't quit an online match before it begins. This is especially annoying when you are put up against a way higher ranked player than you and you can't exit.
-Loading and saving. If this game isn't loading it's saving. If it isn't saving, it's loading.

I could go on and on about the game's cons, but unless you're a hard core fighting gamer, than stay clear away from this game. I am trading in my copy for Batman Arkham City or anything else really.

text:

It has a card for getting bubbles out, but it's a little flimsy and I wound up using an old credit card instead to much better effect. I botched the first application, but was able to lift the cover up, smooth out the bubbles, and lay it back down without the adhesive losing much integrity, but if you totally ruin the first one, there is another one included if you need it.

So far, the glass has held up well both docked and undocked for hours and hours of gameplay and I haven't seen any warping or other signs of wear.

title: Fun game would have been better without the toys
text:
I thought the concept was cool, and that the actual game itself was really well made but that the toys kind of took away from the game play. When I opened the box I was actually really kind of excited about the toys aspect of it, it was definitely an interesting concept. I liked the starter ship and how you could alter it based on what you had plugged into it. The thing that bummed me out the most about the toys was that you have to pay to get new parts of whatever, so this is one of those games that are a bit of an investment and I didn’t enjoy the toy aspect enough to want to make that kind of investment.
About the gameplay, it was good, I enjoyed it. The controls are really fluid and intuitive. The air combat was really good, a lot of times those things made me motion sick, but this didn’t. The graphics were nice. The story was good and it kept me entertained. The game would have been rated better for me if you could customize without the toys.

title: PROS and CONS- Updated
text:
Im usually very critical when it comes to products. But when they work and they are good, I give them their due. I rather NOT spend 100 bucks on this thing. But it works and it works well. It upgrades your consoles whether your console directly outputs via HDMI or has to go through upscaler like an OSSC. It improves the visuals output from every single console from retro to ps4. The colors generally are richer and images are cleaner with more depth.

For example, I have a RGB modded Genesis Model 1 Non TMSS with every improvement you can think of to soup it up to get the best visuals possible. The problem is the tech is old and so you are prone to some blurriness when random motion occurs. If you are used to slow paced games, then you wont get the max benefit from it, but you still will because of how much it cleans up the signal making it look nearly HD. Most reviewers show static pictures or pre-recorded intros rather than actually playing on the thing to show how effective it is.

title: SKIP this game- NOT necessary to play Nier Automata.
text:
This game couldve been so good, but it turned out to be somewhat of a poor game. First the good. Combat mechanics are fun, not great like dark souls, but its fun. The magic spells are fun to use and execute throughtout the game. The ability to change out spells in mid combat makes it not a complete real-time combat, but thats fine. Its a nice compromise considering you are limited to using a joystick. The graphics are good for its time, if not a little gray. But it becomes really good and the colors and motion become much richer and fluid with an upscaler.

The bad: Dialogue, I appreciate that they are trying to wax poetical but its too verbose. I understand that they had alot to say, and alot of ideas, but they werent organized very well. Its also not elegantly written either. Its just all over the place. That being said, it does have to be translated so its probably better in Japanese. If you take a look at games like Demon's souls, Dark souls, Bloodborne, you dont have to write volumes to get the point across that life is harsh, brutal and cold, but with some beauty sprinkled into what we call life that sometimes makes it all seem worthwhile. Souls series does it through focusing intensely on creating a visual atmosphere and sparse dialogue that hints at what is. But what this series does is try to expound verbally, what can hardly be expressed through words. Even the epilogue is completely verbal. Could they not just throw in some animations to carry the message and make it worth watching?

That brings me to the next huge negative- Kaine. She could arguably be the most annoying supporting character Ive run across. Even her walking around half naked couldn't make up for it. She could even beat the handler in Monster Hunter World. The only saving grace is that you don't hear Kaine all the time unlike the handler. And at least in the PC version of monster hunter world you can mute her and even change her face. Thank goodness for that. In any case, I understand what they were trying to do, make a volatile, seemingly complex character, likeable by helping the player empathize with her background through small but meaningful moments throughout the game. But no, it just fails to work. Perhaps the Japanese version works, but this utterly fails imo.

The last negative- Music. Sound quality is fine. but the music is so repetitive. If they were going to recycle the same music over and over again, could they not use low impact, no vocal instrumentals? Or just use it once in a while to create a nice, lasting impact? Its fine to hear the full track a few times, but over and over again, it just becomes hard to bear. This is really a huge negative as music is a huge part of any game. They need to master things like this, which I will say, in the newest Nier Automata game, they seem to have done. So bravo for that.

All in all, this game is not necessary to play Nier Automata, a complete standaline, which so far plays like a masterpiece of a game in all areas. You can avoid this game and really not miss a thing.

title: State of the games today.
text:
This game is a prime example of what is wrong with today's game industry - it's absolutely confused. Its a perfect representation of what is going on today in more ways than one. It tries to appeal to everyone and in the end, the result is horrendous. Its a game with little imagination, it trivializes everything, the tone is completely off, the dialogue will set you back a few dozen IQ points. The game just doesn't take itself seriously, and frankly you shouldn't either. I received this game for free after upgrading my video card. Im usually a completionist but I could not bear to finish it after the first chapter.

Go play games like halo, dead space and bio shock (not the sequels) and you will understand. If you haven't played it in a while, Id suggest you try again. Great serious, story telling with fun game mechanics. Ive replayed them recently and it reminded me how terrible much of the games are today.

The pros- Wolfenstein's graphics are nice. I ran it in ultra-wide multi-monitor setup without a hitch. But on a 2080ti, I expect it to do so. Game mechanics ran fine. About the only positives I can think of. So it gets 2 stars for the visuals and that it ran smoothly.

I cant believe this is my first amazon review and its about this game. Its honestly not worth my time, but I didnt want anyone else to waste theirs. Maybe itll snowball, into a revolt against game makers of this ilk-just wishful thinking. But if it helps one person thats good enough for me. In any case, Id suggest moving on and looking for something else.

title: Bluetooth Connection is Not Reliable and Headphones Keep Shutting Down
text:
I got these headphones for my husband, who games occasionally and who was also looking for a set that would double as a high-fidelity, comfortable wireless set of headphones that also did Bluetooth for use when he is teleworking. He freely admits that he finds the headphones very comfortable, and the sound excellent. A lot of his calls are long distance; some even come from out of the country, and the sound is not always sterling. He was also pleased with the fact that the boom mike works flawlessly and his callers could hear him clearly and there was little request for him to repeat himself.

However, the Bluetooth has been a total disappointment. On the first day it took some time for the headphones to initially connect to his cell phone (a Google Pixel). He is usually taking calls one after the other, but after each call he must write a report where he is not actually using the Bluetooth, and also, at this time of year, people do not call as much because they are away for the holidays. So, as he waited for his calls to come in or as he wrote his reports up, the headphones would regularly shut themselves off after a pre-determined period of time. This seems like an energy-saving feature that I'm sure is helpful when you are gaming so you don't waste your battery charge, but if you have to be immediately available for a telephone call, it is definitely detrimental. He would slip the headphones off and turn them back on each time it happened, but this gets annoying having to do it over and over every 20 minutes or every half hour or whatever the time period was (he didn't time it). [I timed it after connecting the headphones to my Acer laptop. If you don't use the headphones after 20 minutes, they power down.] However, the moment he did turn the headphones back on, the Bluetooth immediately reconnected. So he did use them for the remainder of the day.

However, the next day he had the same difficulty connecting with the Bluetooth initially, and when the headphones shut themselves off automatically and he reconnected, the Bluetooth did not automatically reconnect. This happened several times, which was the final straw and he went back to using his old headphones.

I wondered if this problem stemmed from not having loaded the Turtle Beach app. Perhaps there was some way to turn off the energy-saving feature. That would solve all his problems. However, I did not find that option on the app after loading it on his phone.

In short, the sound is excellent as is the delivery from the boom mike. But the Bluetooth is not reliable, so we cannot give these headphones a good rating.

(If someone knows how to keep the headphones from shutting off while being used for Bluetooth only, please let us know! He was pleased otherwise with the headphones and would love to give them a higher rating.)

title: It's more than you'd think for the price
text:
Considering the favored astrology software cost as much as my new laptop, WinStar was a relief to find. I thought I'd just be able to cast a natal chart, maybe do transits and synastry charts. Even though one can cast charts at astro.com for free there's times when there is no WiFi where I'm giving an astrology reading. I needed software installed on my new HP Laptop. Budgets being what they are for me I "settled" on WinStar.

I didn't expect what I found, a little treasure of an astrology program, and believe me I've been using astrology software since back in the day when I had to Boss my DOS, ok?

What I found that surprised me:

A second disc with tutorials for the beginner, and it's good to have as a reference even if you're not a beginner.

Atlas: An atlas that I've not been able to stump yet.

Reports: Natal, Transit, Synastry and Progressed reports that you can generate and save as pdf or text files, that you can email as an attachment to yourself or your client. BIG PLUS!

Wheels galore: An assortment of wheel types, single, double, different house systems. You can also email those.

To email wheel charts or reports hit "print" and it goes to a pdf format, from there you can save, print, or email. When I'm out and about doing astrology readings in a cafe with WiFi I can email the wheel and report to my client as something to refer to when they get home. I also email myself the same material for the client's folder on my home desk top. If I am not where there's WiFi I can burn the report to a DVD disc with my laptop and hand the disc to the client right there, on the beach, in the forest, under ground in a bunker.

When doing a double wheel the transit option comes up automatically. Nifty! If you want to select another chart for synasty you can do that but I like that the transit option comes up first.

Transit "Time Line": It's transits done for 3 days, 1 week, 1 month, 1 year, as a multi-colored ribbon, the dates run along this "time line". It shows when planets go into a new sign, or transit a new house for the client. It shows the transiting planets aspecting the natal planets in one color, progressed planets are shown in another color, solar arch are shown in another color. If you ever had a client ask just how long transiting Saturn is going to be opposed their natal Moon you can easily see it on this time line. One draw back is you can't do a time line for the current day, like if you just wanted to do general forecasts. The work around is to cast the birth data for yesterday, do the time line for a week or a month and you can have the information you need.

I know I have not exhausted the possibilities of this software. Don't let the price fool you. It's not light weight. It has helped me a great deal when doing readings away from home in my laptop and away from WiFi if that's the environment I find myself. I'm very pleased.

title: Returned after 1 day
text:
I bought this on Wednesday, paid $18 for 1 day shipping, received it Thursday, used it Thursday night for a couple of hours. The light really does not reach the far corner. I thought, I could live with that for the convenience of having a Kindle case with a built in light.

I used the Kindle in the case on Friday for less than an hour while out on errands. On the way home on the bus I get a "Low Battery" notice. My new Kindle 3 was fully charge and had only been used a few hours before I got the case. I had the WiFi off which was supposed to save battery life.

I did a search online about Kindle low battery and found many people who have their Kindles in the "Official" Amazon Kindle case, with or without a light, had battery drain. That the battery drained even if you weren't using it, WiFi off, sitting in a drawer. I was wondering why it was taking so long to recharge while in the case and I read that one person had LESS battery charge after recharging the Kindle in the case over night. That's unacceptable. So after having the case w/light for one day I'm returning it. It will cost me another $7.00 out of my refund for shipping it back. I spent $25 to experience the Official Amazon Kindle Case with Light. This is the first item I've returned to Amazon. The return process was easy I must admit.

Update: I am being refunded the $18.00 for one day shipping. Nice! Again I will say that Amazon.com's return and refund process is very good. Now if they can tweak the Kindle case w/light so it wasn't a battery drain we'd purchase it again.
