title: Click click click, this is responsive and clean
text:
During my very first typing class in 7th grade, I had an instantaneous awe of the way I could press a button and the letter or number on that key would appear on paper. Older computer keyboards felt a little similar but not the same, really, you know like when you're thinking and rub your fingers on the keys. If you type a lot or enjoy gaming on a computer, responsiveness is critical for speed and comfort. With the tactile but pretty quiet keys on the [[ASIN:B00N2ROO2S Corsair Gaming K70 RGB LED Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Cherry MX Red (CH-9000068-NA)]], I'm brought back to the days when I typed on that old typewriter and even though the area of the keyboard is smaller, I'm in heaven.

For gamers, this keyboard will likely take you to heaven. Since the K70 is now in RGB, you can set it up with colors beyond the imagination and save your profile/s for play on any machine. For non-gamers, the RGB is not really necessary, but it sure adds another dimension if you type, as I do, in the dark. If you don't want the keys lit, you can dim them or turn them off.

The black aluminum case of the Cherry MX Red version which I have is classy to look at and impressive to hold. I especialy love the right angled corners and I use the removable wrist rest which has a texture that is smooth, almost leathery. On a table or desk, I can keep it flat and rely on the rubber strips to hold it in place or I can raise it with four simple feet. Right now, I'm typing with it on my lap and I have the computer on a chair a few feet away. Although the quick start guide says I must use both of the two USB plugs, I have simply plugged in the one with the keyboard on it and it's working fine. For gaming or utilizing more than just typing or with a computer of USB 1 or USB2, both plugs are needed, but with a USB3 port on the computer, the single works fine.

A complete manual really should be downloaded and if you've ordered this keyboard, you can do that while waiting for it to be delivered, so you'll be ready when you take it out of the nice looking box. I know that some people have criticized the software, but I have not had problems when I used this on a Windows computer. On the Mac, I was unable to access the Cue software at all. I've switched between a Mac and a Windows based computer and since I saved the profile, it's working fine on both. I am really hoping that Corsair is able to develop for us Mac users.

So, in summary, if you want a mechanical keyboard and use a Windows computer, this is wonderful. If you use a Mac, I'd suggest skipping this RGB version if you love the keyboard and save some money by getting the previous version. The out of the box red LED lights are nice, but you don't need to pay for the color spectrum if you can't access them and some of the functions are not accessible on a Mac. Since I don't really do gaming on the Mac, I'm good.

title: Protection and handy light outweigh its cost
text:
With the reduction in price and the advent of the Special Offer Kindle, countless more will find their ways into the homes of readers all over the world. The Kindle itself would not give a true bibliophile the sensory stimulation of a bound ink on paper book, but this leather lighted cover adds a little bulk to the electronic device making it more resemble a small book in size, while providing protection and illumination.

The Kindle Lighted Leather Cover is lighter in weight than I'd expected, more rigid, better constructed of a high quality beautiful leather, and ergonomically designed for every day use. With care during installation of the Kindle, I expect it to have a long life, particularly since I do not attempt to move the rear cover away from the Kindle device while it's housed. Letting it be and simply lifting the front cover to open, folding it back for reading, and returning it to the closed position for storage should keep it intact. When the front cover is folded back for reading, the round elastic band can be reversed around both front and back covers to keep them joined and make the covered Kindle easier to hold. When the case is closed, the elastic band fits into a small groove on the front of the case where the two different leather textures are seamed. I love that detail. A small leather tab can be slid along the elastic and it also can be flipped to face either right or left. I sometimes move it up or down as a hint to remember something. It has the impression, "amazon kindle," so I'm likely to remember what's in the case. The light is powerful, considering its small size, and it's very easy to pull out and push into it's corner home. It is unobtrusive and quite functional. My brain on more than one occasion guided my hand to the rear of the Kindle for the reading light and it took a few seconds for me to realize I needed to put my fingers on the case and not the Kindle. Because of its angle, the light makes the screen a bit brighter in the upper right quadrant, but my eyes quickly adjust as I read further and become immersed in the words. If I find myself thinking about the irregularity of the lighting on the screen, I go to my Home Page and select another book.

I highly recommend this cover for Kindle owners who want to protect and illuminate their investment and their eyes. Once you make the decision to purchase, good luck when deciding on a color!

title: Definate Click
text:
As my hands age, I have been having more and more issues with keyboard fatigue. Tried many different (non-mechanical) keyboards, including ergonomic keyboards like the Logitech wave, and nothing seemed to help much.

The LEOBOG had a cool name, good price, and great reviews, so I decided to give it whirl. The keys make a nice clicking sound, and provide good feedback, so it is easier to train oneself to not jam down on the keys any harder than necessary, thus minimizing unnecessary impact on the knuckle joints.

Honestly, if you are having issues with your non-mechanical keyboard, I recommend picking up one of these and seeing if it helps you. At $25 it's a perfect gateway mechanical. I have worked in IT for now on 15 years, and hold a very keyboard intensive position within IT. During that time I have tried keyboards from pretty much every manufacturer, and none come close to the feel of this very reasonably priced LEOBOG

It has multicolored lights like pretty much every product of Chinese manufacturers. The good news is that the review of Alyssa Wilson teaches us how to turn that stuff off. She has a big 'ol list of all the different color functions in her awesome review, but below is the one that matters the most. The solid blue is a personal favorite of mine;green is pictured because its the first one that comes up.

FN+PGUP - Solid Color Backlight (FN+F8 Cycles Solid Colors)

title: Buyer Beware
text:
Lowest I can go is one star. Simply: The drivers were not recognized on Windows 10. Although the product page says these released in 2016, there was no download available for the software through digital means (only a disc -- and I was lucky enough to have a drive to quickly connect).

The headset itself refused to be recognized beyond "Generic 7.1 Headset" or something approximate, even after installing the software. The latest drivers from the site (which was a .cc and not the .com stated in the documentation) did not recognize the headset even with the software installed. Likely due to the fact that Windows 10 itself did not recognize the headset.

Strangely, changes the software made to the audio quality did take, even if it was only just recognized as "Generic 7.1 etc". No matter, as both recording and playback were saturated with a constant and grating static sound. I would not recommend these to a Windows 10 user. Especially not when the company FAQ suggests no interest in fixing compatibility with Windows 10. Again, this is supposedly a 2016 product.

title: I'm glad they include two in the package, because I needed both of them to put it on correctly
text:
The glass protector seems to be good quality. The only trouble I had with it was that it's difficult to place it correctly while also getting all the air bubbles out. The instructions included say that pressure applied should start from the center and then be worked outwards. This is extremely difficult to do while also aligning it so there is no overlap over the edges. My first attempt left a sizable air bubble that I couldn't work out to the edge, and I also managed to get a stray piece of fluff or dust under it so I removed it (which is fairly easy to do if you try, and left no residue). My second attempt was much better and I'm happy with the result. You can barely tell there's a protector on there now.

With the protector I removed, I decided to break it just to see how strong it was and it took about a 30-40 degree bend before shattering and putting glass dust everywhere. Seems like it would really protect the screen and I'm glad I have it.

I think this product could be improved by some other guiding strips or something to help with centering, so that the hands are free to start applying pressure from the center to avoid air bubbles.

I think this product could be improved by some other guiding strips or something to help with centering, so that the hands are free to start applying pressure from the center to avoid air bubbles.

Whether longer hours of gaming is a good thing in your life is something you have to decide for yourself, but if you want to game longer one of these will help.

title: Mmm great graphics BUT typical MS programming
text:
OK so after my first session playing... the graphics are astounding, the game play is a little realxing but fun, its sort of Nox meets Unreal and pretends to be Diablo.
But its crashes about once an hour (on a 1ghz Athlon, raid, 32MB ATI, 128MB CAS 2) irregardless of settings. And when I say crash, I mean crash, its brings not only the game but also my usually impervious win2k system to its knees. No task manger, no reset, hard power cycle only!! I dont remeber any of the Diablos crashing ever, or the Baldur's Gates... typical Microsoft, releasing something late and expensive and unfinished!
There are tons of cool ideas in this game but its a bit like the original arcade Dragon's Lair once the wow factor is over you have to live with the limitations...
Everyone should see this game but I wouldn't reccomend anyone actually buy it. If you're short of cash (or sensible about such things) then wait for Neverwinter Nights - most likely a much better investment...

title: Fun simple game
text:
I picked up this game because of the low price and I wanted a filler inbetween some of the Nancy Drew games I like to play. The ND games are very addictive so I thought this might be a simple game that didn't involve too much thinking and would be something to have on hand to play every now and then. Well this game is very addictive and I've only had it a week and I'm almost done with it. It really is a lot of fun. My husband saw me playing and then got into it himself. He's been avoiding it lately because when you start to play, you get hooked and lose track of time.

The good thing about this game is even if you finish the actual game, there is a mode where you can just do endless play that allows to keep going until you lose 4 customers. This records your high score and you can keep playing till you get a higher one. You could acutally do the same with the main game play as well because it keeps adding up the total amount taken in at the restaurant through each level. There is a certain amount you are supposed to earn each level and once you hit that mark, you can try and reach the expert part and that gives you a start for that level. I only got a few stars and there were 2 levels that were so difficult and frusterating that I was just so happy to be past them and didn't care if I reached the expert level or not.

Overall this is a really cute fun little game for all ages. I'm 34 and really enjoy playing it.

title: Fun and challenging
text:
This was the first Nancy Drew game I played and it got me hooked. My husband was walking by during one of the puzzles I was trying to solve and he sat down to see what it was about and ended up playing the entire game with me. We both found this game to be very challenging and addictive. This is a great game for all ages although it might be a little scary for some youngsters.

One thing that we found amusing about this game was a little hidden text. There is a challenge where you will go downstairs to a room (kind of like a lab) and read some letters and notes. This is towards the end of the game. The main part you are supposed to read is darker than the rest of the text. If you strain and read the lighter text, you will see some interesting things there. It's been a while since we played it so I don't remember the exact text but it had to do with views towards the current president. We thought it was amusing that the writer/programmer put that in there.

Overall a great game with some difficult puzzles.

title: Boring and repetitive
text:
I love Sims games, but this one is by far the worst I've ever played. Compared to other sim games, this one is very shallow in terms of the plot and goals. It's highly repetitive (as other reviewers have described as well) as you have to feed and pet animal after animal, area after area, without much else to do. I gave up halfway through because it was becoming so tedious. The graphics and navigation movements are quite crude considering the year this was put out. Also, the rough way the controls are set up to accomodate using the Wii controller (and the wrist movements you have to make to collect and plant seeds, and pet the animals), your hand and wrist can become painful and sore, almost like carpal tunnel.

If you are looking for a cute Sims game, My Sims Kingdom is 10 times better. If you are looking for a fun animal sim game, Viva Pinata is unbeatable.

title: Lovable Cards
text:
After playing my own game included with the New 3ds, I don't feel there is any pressing need for the amiibo cards, since the game itself isn't that deep, and the character's will eventually show up.

I made a mistake on the placement of Katt's house. I didn't realize at the time that I could move it later, so turned it off. When I restarted, I was sad to discover Katt was not there, but other character's were. Maybe this could be used to get your favorite villagers without using the cards.

It's my understanding that only the special character's, like Nook, Isabelle, etc., need the amiibo cards if you desire to decorate their homes. I have purchased a lot of the amiibo cards, but have not felt the need to use one with the game yet. I guess I just don't care enough to use the cards, maybe later. We haven't even played the game in a few days.

The Animal Crossing amiibo cards really are cute. My daughter decided she'd like to collect the set. This has proven to be more of a challenge than I realized. I refuse to pay more than retail for an expensive game add on. I would have liked the option to purchase the complete set as a whole.

The last 6-card set I bought only had one card that wasn't a duplicate. I already regret getting caught up it the collecting. I've spent enough money already. After purchasing 21 sets so far from various stores, I'm about to call it quits. At least I haven't paid more than retail for them. Just be patient, it's not like they won't be restocked.

It came as a huge disappointment when we learned we would not be able to purchase this size after all. After using them I can happily say we are pleased with the smaller size. The only down side is for those that weren't interested in purchasing the game, or the cover plates. Having to spend $220.00 is a high price for anyone only interested in the New 3ds. It's really not a big deal for us because we love Animal Crossing so much.
Of course, the new included game can not compare to the original Animal Crossing game, but it's enjoyable for what it is. We would love to see some of the things from ACHHD included in the next true Animal Crossing game.

title: Love this game wish there were more.
text:
I read all of the reviews before I decided to get this game. I too, like Deepak Chopra and I was excited to find this game.
Some reviews said they got more and more frustrated with each level and found they had to make wild movements to get the game to work.
I didn't find that to be the issue for me at all. I have found this to be a very relaxing game and I feel calm and centered after playing it.
There is a playing mode and and reflection mode for meditation.
On the play mode each level is centered on the chakras starting at the root chakra and moving up. You have a planet that rotates and from the center comes a colored spore that gives birth to a tree or mushroom. Before you start the level you see your mandala begin to pulse in and out and set you breathing to this rhythm, this is also the same rhythm for the remote for the side to side motion to rotate the planet.
And each level progresses in this manner. The point is to cultivate relaxation, the more relaxed you are the easier it is to play the game. I have noticed that when I play other games I don't get so riled up and I can stay calm and relaxed which does make it easier to play and retry a level without frustration. Good tool for the rest of life as well.
Knowing this helps to keep the focus in the game. Once you have gone through the play levels on all the chakras the free style meditation is unlocked, otherwise if you choose the reflection side you have only the guided meditation that is unlocked. I have found these to be very helpful to start my practice again. I sit in a regular chair not on the floor. If I sit on the floor I use a pillow folder over to get the height and stability needed. I find it works just as well.
I am pleased with this game and I continue to use it since I am gaining great benefit from it in all areas of my life. To help me relax I have incorporated an adrenal support that aids in relaxation and have found this has helped immensely.

text:

In overall, this game is pretty satisfying. I'd give it 5 stars. No true gamer can go without playing this!

P.S. Most of these people writing the reviews are just noobs. They aren't far enough in the game to know what the good stuff is!

title: A great protector, or how I learned to banish dust particles from my Switch
text:
Intro

As we all know, the Switch comes with a plastic screen. Whether it was to save money, or to make a more durable product, a plastic screen is obviously very easy to scratch up. This was especially true as putting the Switch inside the dock could easily cause the screen to rub against the side of the dock. Thus, I went ahead and bought this screen protector. It was one of the best reviewed ones at the time, and also one of the best deals, and I am very happy with the purchase.

Durability

I haven't had any issues with durability. I haven't dropped my Switch, but I've taken it on many trips and have yet to see any scratches.

Fit

The fit is very good on the protector. It fits over the entire glossy black area on the switch, including the bezels around the screen itself.

Clarity

I haven't had an issue with this. Most of the time I don't even notice the screen being there.

Application Process

I read through some reviews and many people were having trouble with installation. Since it's such a large screen it's a lot easier to get dust under the protector - one of my pet peeves. My process was to remove any towels and carpets from my bathroom and to steam it up and to do some minor cleaning. Then I sat down with the switch on a table in the bathroom and cleaned the switch and protector carefully with rubbing alcohol to remove dirt and discharge static.
I practiced some dry runs, and then used some canned air to blow dust off the switch and then quickly checked for dust, removed the backing on the protector, and applied it immediately. This resulted in no dust on the first try, which was great.

I have seen that the Switch itself could also be bent a little (it seems like a common problem), so if yours is bent you might have some trouble applying it. In that case it might be better to get a plastic protector.

Conclusion

Overall, a great product and highly recommended. The fact that they include two is an even better bonus in case you break one or fail on an application attempt.

title: Good for Left-Handed Gamers!
text:
This mouse originally came with my RoG G74S a couple of years ago. It's seen a LOT of heavy use, has traveled around the country with me, been dropped, been spilled on and the original now has one button that's a tad "sticky".

As a left handed gamer/mouser with long hands/fingers, this has been the best mouse I've ever used. It fits nicely in my hand and because of the placement of the side buttons, I can use them easily with my ring finger. I appreciate that it doesn't have teeny tiny buttons too small for even toddler fingers to press singly, but rather nice sized buttons that won't having accidentally casting (and wasting) a spell/ability.

The new RoG mouse doesn't feel the same in my hand and has different button placement - it may have been a matter of being used to this one and not giving the new mouse enough play time to get used to it, but I switched back to this mouse and ordered a 2nd for when this one bites the dust.

title: Swamp ear
text:
These are the nicest headphones I've ever experienced. Here's what I liked about them.

1. Sound quality. I didn't realize how tinny and flat my old ones were until I tried these. I guess part of the difference is the tight suction over the ears that blocks out everything or it could be the speakers.

2. Durability. Well, I've been using them for a month, once I sat on them, black headphones on a black seat! But they are still working and I haven't managed to break the speaker, perfection!

Here's what I don't like.

1. Hot Ear. I haven't run out to buy canned air or tried my hand at inventing cooling gel ear muffs, but so far I can't wear these for more than an hour at a time without getting super sweaty hot ears. It's sorta swampy and gross like spandex butt, 'cept its on your head. The headphones really clamp down on your head and sometimes the tension can make my head hurt.

But other than the head pain and itchy swamp ear, these are pretty great. Good luck!

That said, the entertainment value of this game more than makes up for this deficiency, and it is still a must have game.

title: A golf game that makes you laugh. Not for serious golfers.
text:
Retiree here. After reaching pro level on Wii golf, I wanted to play a different golf game. The same course (Wii golf) is too repetitive. I agree with the other 2 reviews posted to date. Just purchased it, have played for 2 hours, and will update this ASAP. It's a fun game with very good graphics. I have not read the directions yet, (like to jump in and play first), and found swinging confusing until I realized how it works. You lift your club until the blue line on the power bar, equals the distance you need to drive. Totally different than Wii golf, and should not be confused with a real golf match game. However, there is enough golf, and interesting scenery, to satisfy my desire for a second game. This game is a sleeper, and will get much more playing time than some other titles I have reviewed.

While Miis are not used, the characters are a definite plus. They are lifelike humans, rather than cartoonish. When you have some winnings, you take your character to the clubhouse, and dress them as you like. The costumes range from conservative to highly suggestive. I wasn't able to purchase the new clothing, but I was able to change my character into the different outfits. Initially, you only have a choice of 2 characters. I am using Hanah, a cute and personable girl of about 20. She has a cute voice. Based on my initial 3 hole practice round (done 4 times until my first birdie), I expect to put quite a few hours on this game.

This is my update. I have now read the directions. Marginal help. Then I went through the tutorial again. I was making a lot of mistakes. You need to go through the tutorial a second time. It means more after you have played. You can change the direction of your putts and drives, just like Wii golf. The special shots are fun. I just finished 3 more hours of play. The game is addictive, once you understand it. You have to like humor. I like Rayman Rabbits. I think 8 years and up is an appropriate age level. Girls 8+ will especially like the different costumes and accessories available. Boys will just like the game play. It's also great for adults. I'm a retiree. The key is to go through the tutorial several times. Once before you play. then at least once after you have played for 1-2 hours. I was initially frustrated before I went back to the tutorial. I think this is a great game and will be playing it quite a bit.

title: Enjoyable. Generates laughter like Rayman 1.
text:
Retiree here (retired CPA, Professor). New to gaming. Started with my Wii purchase, Dec 31, 2007). I play these games solo. Wife won't play them (other than Wii Sports-she's addicted to that one). title: Cute story about a writer struggling for independance
text:
My main interest in this movie was the story of Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings. She is a writer who is leaving her life to pursue her writing dreams and find fulfillment in publishing a novel.

Her husband is not interested in her dreams. She decides to seek solitude in an isolated orange grove in Florida. Little does she know, this will not be an ideal life. After 30 years of urban life, she is not prepared for a small Florida town.

After many rejections, Marjorie finally realizes "Gothic Novels" are not her specialty. Her agent helps her see how interesting her life actually is and she begins to write about what she knows best. In the process she falls in love, makes a best-friend, helps the community by hiring everyone who lives around her to help remodel her house and fix up her orchard.

Cross Creek is based on the best-selling memoirs of Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings and has some very human moments when you realize the beauty or ugliness of life. The local business man (Peter Coyote) who falls in love with her, does something so amazing. It reminded me of when my father bought my mother her first car. title: Finally wireless freedom while maintaining traditional gaming expectations
text: So to answer the question at the start, Yes this is a good mouse and no wireless doesn't hold it back from maintaining gaming performance. I'm coming from an older logitech gaming mouse the G500 which I've used and enjoyed for years due to it's ergonomics and gaming performance. I've always enjoyed the G500 so this Logitech G403 does carry many of the similar ergonomics as well as overall feel. The surface of the mouse has a nice soft touch plastic which gives it a good grip as well as comfort for longer use sessions. Not having a wire is really fantastic, as that was one of the drawbacks to the G500 in that the wire would often make you feel restricted when moving the mouse in specific directions. By default the G403 does feel really light, but comes with a weight to install which I would recommend using. I've not played around with the RGB lighting as of yet, but it does cycle through a gamut of colors so you could easily tailor the colors to match your pc lighting or match an rgb keyboard. The build quality is top notch, and the cable has a nice sleeve for a clean appearance. To charge the mouse you need to connect the mouse to the cable itself and it will allow you to use the mouse as a corded option while charging if you would prefer which is a great option for Logitech to have included. The mouse is super responsive and the buttons have a satisfying click to them and I've not noticed any increased latency in games while using the mouse wirelessly. Overall I'm very satisfied with this mouse and glad that I can finally have the freedom of wireless gaming without having to sacrifice either performance or comfort!

text: This game has two characters to choose from.  The plot is the same, it revolves around murders that occurred 17 years ago and seem to be happening again.  The great thing about this game is the character plot is not the same.  If you choose Ellen (the easier version) you travel down one path.  If you choose the reporter (the harder version)it takes you down a completely different path.  You can play both players.  You battle the same bosses, but your interactions with people are different and your clues are different and your 'IDs' (ie, the animals you fight with are different) thus your strategy on how to beat the bosses are different.  As there is alway two sides to a story, one character follows one side and the other character follows the other side.  I am only on the 3rd chapter out of five.  At this point the characters have choosen sides and are at cross roads with each other.  In the beginning they started out helping each other.  Anyway, this has been a unique and fun game so far.

title: not ready for release...
text:
not ready or defective. not sure because oculus tech support was fail.

I'm actually sad I had to send mine back and get a refund. It was almost an awesome product.

But oculus tech support did not do the needful. I'm certain the issue was the cable included with the headset. Lots of snow and static on screen that didnt show up in a screen mirror on your real screen.

Was ignored and treated very poorly by oculus support. After almost a month of using I frantically boxed it up and sent it back to amazon.

I think I might pick up another from best buy and see if it does the same thing or not. I tested 3 high end vr pcs with it btw. But either way. I feel let down by oculus support. And Amazon didnt offer replacement of item. They only offer return or dealing with oculus. So I realized I better return this thing asap!

I wish they were being more honest about the issues as I would repurchase once issues are fixed.

Biggest let down with this device is trying to play non vr games in a vr theater. It absolutely does not work! The oculus drivers upscale everything into 4k even if the monitor being displayed is only 1920x1080... this results in unbearable stutter in the majority of non vr games. And this is something that an oculus go can handle over wifi with open source software like alvr and moonlight for go so I am shocked to see they dropped the ball so badly by not having a 1080p theater gaming mode.... it's actually unforgivable and I think I would have returned this item due to that fact alone if I wasnt having the USB power and snow static issues....

I think they rushed the software and the skimped on costs for a high quality cable...

title: I like it better than the New 3DS XL
text:
I bought a New 3DS XL a while back, but quickly learned that it was a little bulky for my liking and I was noticing that I was having a bit of fatigue in my hands and wrists. I really wanted the smaller device, but I didn't want to sacrifice the benefits of the new 3ds (better 3d and the C-nub). I was also excited about the interchangeable faceplates.

When I bought this device, it was the only North American option for a non-XL, so while I wasn't really into Animal Crossing, I was very into the smaller device, and since the faceplates are interchangeable, it wasn't a big deal to me (though I do wish that this bundle included the plain white plates as well).

I shopped around and found a great deal online where I got this bundle for under $180 on Jet, so this was really a no-brainer.

I do find that I still get some hand strain, not because of weight, but because of the way I hold the console; my hands are just slightly too big for long use comfort (typically, I get strain after about 1.5 hours of use).

The new 3D face tracking is a big step up from the original 3DS. The C-stick is not used for happy home designer, but has been useful in the handful of games that have C-stick functionality.

I like the layout of this console better. The cartridge in front design seems more ergonomic than the last 3DS, which had it in back where your fingers naturally lie.

Overall, I think the New 3DS is a wonderful, polished console. It is the perfect size for travel. The new features increase the options for game developers (ZL/ZR buttons, c-stick). The new 3D face tracking makes using 3D more immersive and less of a practice of patience. As for the Happy Home Designer, I don't really have any interest, but all of those components are interchangeable, and the game arrives as a code that can be given to someone who will actually use it (it is not locked to the device).

I have no regrets with my purchase of this console. If I had list any complaint is that the new 3DS consoles do not come with the power supply.

title: Wonderful, but not without some faults!
text:
I enjoy the occasional game and decided I wanted to get back into handheld gaming. While cell phone games do have plenty of engaging time-killing games to offer, I was missing games with some depth and story; like Zelda! So I decided to go back to my roots and get a Nintendo console (my roots are the old DMG-1).

After a shockingly small amount of research, I went and impulse purchased the New 3DS XL. If this is your first 3DS, be sure to pick up a charger as well, since, unlike just about any other device that NEEDS a charger, this system does not come with one! Taking the device out of the box, the first thing you will notice is the pristine shiny surfaces that greet you! The exterior is shiny, but don't expect it to stay pretty. It will pick up finger prints if you just look at it. Not only that, but I had scratches on it after a couple weeks of keeping it in my bag (in a pocket that was microfiber lined and all by itself).

Next thing you will notice is the weight. This device actually has some heft to it! It is only 1 or 2 tenths of an ounce lighter than the original Nintendo! I found that I did get a but of hand and wrist strain during the first could days of play. Just something to keep in mind!

Another thing you will notice is that the hinge is a bit flappy. When you open the hinge, you will hear it snap into place in two positions (and by snap, it sounds and feels like you are doing something wrong). This wouldn't be a problem since the second position is where you will want the screen opened to, but the screen moves within that position. I play a lot from a reclined or laying position, so I do notice the top screen wobbling quite a bit. I would estimate that the movement is about 5 degrees. It is enough that, if I am playing while laying down, I often find myself awkwardly positing my index fingers so they wrap around to the front of the device to keep it from moving while I am playing. I have seen video of New 3DS XLs that do not have this issue with the hinge, but most people seem to have it, and people who have contacted Nintendo say that Nintendo does not consider this to be a defect.

Even with all of the negatives I have listed, there is still so much to love about this device. The top screen is beautiful and sharp. The Super Stable 3D does great (even when you play in the dark). The console comes with a few interesting games, so even if you don't by games right away, there is definitely lots of interesting stuff to do on the device. The e-shop is great and even has some great games that you can get for relatively cheap including some old NES and Gameboy games. The controls are generally ergonomic, although I find that the D-pad can be a little uncomfortable if you are playing a game that uses that instead of letting you use the thumb pad. Streetpass and spotpass add a whole other dimension of entertainment. There are a lot of great games available for the system for almost any genre. All the old Nintendo franchises have games for the 3DS that have a terrific balance between familiar characters and new spins on gameplay that develop the story.

If this is your first 3DS, be sure to pick up a charger as well, since, unlike just about any other device that NEEDS a charger, this system does not come with one! Taking the device out of the box, the first thing you will notice is the pristine shiny surfaces that greet you! The exterior is shiny, but don't expect it to stay pretty. It will pick up finger prints if you just look at it. Not only that, but I had scratches on it after a couple weeks of keeping it in my bag in a pocket that was microfiber lined and all by itself . Next thing you will notice is the weight. This device actually has some heft to it! It is only 1 or 2 tenths of an ounce lighter than the original Nintendo! I found that I did get a but of hand and wrist strain during the first could days of play. Just something to keep in mind! Another thing you will notice is that the hinge is a bit flappy. When you open the hinge, you will hear it snap into place in two positions and by snap, it sounds and feels like you are doing something wrong . This wouldn't be a problem since the second position is where you will want the screen opened to, but the screen moves within that position. I play a lot from a reclined or laying position, so I do notice the top screen wobbling quite a bit. I would estimate that the movement is about 5 degrees. It is enough that, if I am playing while laying down, I often find myself awkwardly positing my index fingers so they wrap around to the front of the device to keep it from moving while I am playing. I have seen video of New 3DS XLs that do not have this issue with the hinge, but most people seem to have it, and people who have contacted Nintendo say that Nintendo does not consider this to be a defect. Even with all of the negatives I have listed, there is still so much to love about this device. The top screen is beautiful and sharp. The Super Stable 3D does great even when you play in the dark . The console comes with a few interesting games, so even if you don't by games right away, there is definitely lots of interesting stuff to do on the device. The e-shop is great and even has some great games that you can get for relatively cheap including some old NES and Gameboy games. The controls are generally ergonomic, although I find that the D-pad can be a little uncomfortable if you are playing a game that uses that instead of letting you use the thumb pad. Streetpass and spotpass add a whole other dimension of entertainment. There are a lot of great games available for the system for almost any genre. All the old Nintendo franchises have games for the 3DS that have a terrific balance between familiar characters and new spins on gameplay that develop the story.

Don't worry that it is a Japan import! Nintendo didn't have region codes associated with games or consoles at the time, so every game you have will still work, no matter where it came from!

I got this console very quickly (3 weekdays)! It only had minor cosmetic scratches and what looked like battery acid in a couple crevices (but the battery contacts looked pristine). It runs great!

title: Destiny, but way better
text: There was a point early in The Division where I found the remnants of a voicemail left by a daughter trapped in the city and facing eminent death. She was calling her parents to tell them — emotionally and with her voice slurring from the few drinks she admitted to having imbibed to gain the courage to make the call — that she was gay and this was why she had moved to New York in the first place, to find a more accepting community. It was at that point, where I was listing to this message while also ducking behind cover to avoid the gunfire from looters, that The Division hooked me. I am a big fan of Destiny, a game The Division shares a lot with in terms of a persistent online world, but in that one moment The Division showed more story than Destiny's entire campaign, The Taken King expansion included. Up until this point it was kind of a nonchalant "Yah, take back New York, whatever." Now, however, the game had weight. You aren't fighting against some vague alien presence that for one reason or another is mad at the human race but everyone is too busy to explain why they are too busy to explain it to you, you are fighting for these people whose lives were suddenly uprooted. That's what makes The Divsion great. Ohh and the matchmaking is much better too.

title: An Experience Unlike Any Other
text:
It’s about as easy to describe the game Journey to someone as it is to describe Doctor Who. You love it, you know why you love it, but to put it into words is nearly impossible. While describing your love for Doctor Who may make you sound certifiably insane, trying to describe Journey makes it sound boring, which it is certainly far from. Yet, despite that potentiality, I will do my best to paint a more detailed picture as to why we still love it and will continue to love it for years to come.

You’ve probably heard from so many mouths that Journey (crafted by thatgamecompany) is “touching” and “beautiful” to the point where it almost sounds cliche, but it’s true. This game genuinely provides you with an experience unlike that which you could have with any other game. I haven’t played it in nearly two years, and yet I can still remember precisely how I felt when I reached the end.

This is going to sound cheesy, so prepare yourself, but you don’t play Journey to have fun, you play Journey to be moved and to be taken on a ride you’ve never been on before. If you end up having fun anyway, then that’s great, but sitting down to play Journey is more like going to a museum of art, as opposed to strapping in for a day at the theme park.

I don’t want to spoil the ending for you, but to sum up, it pretty much falls into the categories of: unforgettable, shocking, moving, touching, resonating, and sobering. It will put a smile on your face moments after it makes you cry, and you will come to understand how you can bond on a deeper level with a real person whom you’ve never met. And single player is not an option - well, at least at certain points. You’ll understand why when you play.

While you may delightfully frolic with your anonymous companion on your mission to get to the mountain (located at the end of what seems like the largest desert imaginable), you can do nothing more than jump or speak to each other in song, something that would, in reality, be more than sufficient, should we ever end up alone on such a quest - a quest that becomes more evident by the end of the game and will have you nodding in approval.

Under any other circumstances, Journey would probably suck. But it’s with those kid gloves with which thatgamecompany makes all of their games, including flOw (a subtle game of evolution) and Flower (where you control flower petals on the wind), that make their gaming experiences more of an interactive meditation than a traditional gaming session. You play games like Call of Duty and God of War to release your aggression, but you pick up a thatgamecompany game to soothe your soul.

The fact that Journey is an indie title makes it even more impressive that it was so memorable, though less surprising that it is as profound. The visuals are breathtaking, particularly the glimmering pink sands, and the soft sounds are unlike any you’ve heard before in a video game. Journey is the perfect example of why you don’t need a lot of glitz and glamour - sometimes less truly is more...so much more.

title: Solid Game from the Franchise
text: Dynasty Warriors 8 essentially plays like every other Dynasty Warriors game.  Read as: you don't play for the plot, you play to level up your weapons and your attack power so that you can take down foes in one hit.  Thankfully, the beautifully rendered cut scenes (which, while appreciated, are slowing our progress), can be skipped, though there is an option on one of the boards in the Wei dynasty where, if you play it a certain way, you can unlock new dialogue for Lu Bu.  I can't imagine anyone racing to do that.  Anyway, the generals, of course, have musou, too, and here they'll take you out in one clip, even if you have full health.  So unless you are seriously packing heat, you might want to stay out of the way until they're done raging.  In "Story" mode, you can play through each dynasty to unlock boards and characters that you can then play on "Free" mode, which is normally a less than satisfying mode in other games, but since we're not here for the plot, "Free" mode is a great way to level up your favorite character., as well as their respective weapons.  Though, you don't have to stick to the weapons you're given - you can choose from any on the list.  One annoying thing about this, though, is that you do not land, by default, on your character's weapon when you choose the list.  You have to scroll down until you see the "EX" next to the weapon - that's how you know you're on your character's default weapon.  But don't feel limited by that - you can mix and match the "elements" of different weapons to provide better attacks (though, of course, your default weapon will give you a specific attack that only your character can do).  You can also use animal accompaniments which come with their own perks, depending on the sidekick you choose.  There's also "Ambition" mode, which is new to the series, and here you can build up a town, but not in the "Farmville" engine that every app seems to come with these days.  You make the area stronger by participating in various battles, and these battles will either give you materials to construct the Tongquetai Tower, fame, or new partners.  Later on, you can also unlock a co-op version of "Ambition" mode.  My favorite character is "Flute Chick," a.k.a. Zhang He, and while her attacks are purple and pretty, her musou was a bit of a let-down.  Plus, you don't get to unlock her until much later, which leads me to believe that she's one of everyone else's favorites as well.  All in, it's a solid game, and it doesn't fall short of what you would expect from the Dynasty Warriors series.

title: Fun game
text:
007 Nightfire is out for all major platforms, in time for the latest Bond film. The graphics are stunning, gameplay is amazing. Well worthy of the series!
I'm a huge fan of the Bond games, and we have all of the previous ones. We got this one as soon as it came out, and were definitely not disappointed!
The graphics are a huge step up from previous versions. In the first 'training' mission, you're driving a car through city streets. The lights reflect off of the curves of the car, you can see inside to all of his controls and movements, the dents show up realistically, the back up lights glow softly, and if you bash it a bit, the trunk comes loose. The city around you has cobblestone streets, water rippling, streetlights that come down when you hit them. The attention to detail is just amazing!
As you then move on through the various levels, you see this same level of detail everywhere. From the Austrian castle and other alpine scenes, to the city scenes, watery scenes and more, each really shines.
The plot is very engaging and typically Bond. But in an attempt to show that this isn't about violence - he's a SPY after all, not a Rambo - you get bonus points for being stealthy instead of blasting in with guns, and for stunning or capturing enemies instead of killing them.
In fact, just about every area can be 'accomplished' in many ways. Bluster your way into an objective by a full frontal assault ... or sneak in the side way for extra points. Since you're also rewarded for your time and health, often the sneaky, non-violent way is the best.
You've got a huge array of equipment, weapons, armor and vehicles, and all work just the way you'd expect them to. I found the default controller configuration REALLY annoying, but a quicks stop in the config area got it back to the way I'm used to playing.
Plus, there's multiplayer! Play with up to four people at once on REALLY great maps with quite a bit of customization options on each one. Grab some bots for practice, and play arena, team arena, king of the hill, capture the flag, or other game types.
Definitely worthy of the Bond series, and highly, highly recommended to any first person shooter fan!

title: Good sound, too big for me
text:
These headphones work well. The sound is good. Not fantastic, but good. The headphones do well with low sound, like bass. But they're a bit cloudy on the mid and high tones.

I like the cool lights on the sides. I haven't used the mic yet.

I wish they plugged in with a regular headphone jack so I could use them for other things than computer gaming. The USB plug limits that. I guess I could get an adaptor?

My only real complaint is that they're very large on me. They have a flexible strap to adjust them to different sizes of heads. Being a small female, that strap sits way below the top of the headband, leaving a big gap in between. They look a bit ridiculous on. But for people larger than me, this is probably a good selling point they will fit much larger heads than most headphones I'm used to. and the harde plastic part won't touch, only the flexible band.

title: Frustratingly difficult. Despite anything you do, you're punished!
text:
I've been playing the game for the last 3 days, and I'm about to just give up in frustration. A game is supposed to be fun, isn't it?

My Player mode is extremely unforgiving difficult game.
Part of the goal of the mode is to be a good team mate and work your way up as a starter. To do that, you do the nitty gritty things like set screens for your players. This works, only sometimes, and other times the AI players simply just stand there. Wasting time, waiting for your ballhandler to make a move. I'm begging the AI to come on, please start the play! We'll talk about being hypocritical in a moment here.
Playing as point guard, you get punished for holding the ball too long, by a large margin. Hey now, I'm trying to survey the floor looking for a good pass! Oh hey, a player is cutting towards the basket so I'll pass the ball to him. But oops! He continues running around the opponent and they intercept or tip the ball. Bass pass penalty, major points lost. What? So what is it? Do I take my time looking for the players to stop running and get the good pass or do I try to rush a pass to a running player?
Playing defense is brutal as well. You can't stand in close because the opponent will run right past you leaving you chasing them. Or you can't stand back a bit and they'll just shoot a jumper over you. Is there even anything we can do to prevent the major lost of points for allowing your man to score?
Okay well another problem is deciding who to defend running back after your team misses a shot. Well, hmm, the player defending arrows is pointing one way.. okay I'll go head there to defend. If you rely on the blue circles around opponents to defend, well, good luck because sometimes there are two players which you need to defend at once. Huh? WHAT? Okay, let's pick our position to defend instead. Makes sense right? Wait why is my team mate defending this guy too? The open opponent who just scored was the guy you were supposed to defend. You just lost a major amount of team mate points. Okay now we're chasing a fast breaking opponent down. There are 2 other team mates in front of him and the guy still makes the basket....just trying to help out, but yes more penalties to the team mate score. Oh also, sometimes the passes don't go to the right guy as well.

Whatever you do, you're going to get penalized. It's extremely frustrating.

There's probably more things I've forgot to mention that's wrong with this game, but let's close up this review. I realize I've ranted long enough already.

Another major issue is that it loads slowly. Can't the game play the cut scenes while loading? You simply have to wait out the load times, and watch the cut scenes that are forced on you, for the hundredth time. Get me into the game please!

I mean, parts of the game can be fun when you get to play but there are some really difficult things to master, like the shooting timing, the freethrow timing, the idiotic penalties. Don't add on to the frustration with it being just so darn slow to load. And come on, don't throw the player in there on Pro difficulty with no chance to learn the system. Why don't they have rookie enabled for My Player, I don't know.

I give up on you NBA 2K11. Maybe I'll try 2K12 when prices drop to more reasonable level.

title: Comfortable communicator for  Xbox pals.
text: This lightweight Titanfall 2 Official Marauder Six Four Communicator for Xbox One works great. I hooked it up to my iPhone and my laptop and made volume adjustments on each until I got perfection. I highly recommend that you read the instruction booklet that comes with this Communicator, otherwise, you will most likely not get the volume adjustment and the off on to work very well. Also, when using your Xbox, make sure you adjust that volume accordingly on your tv for optimal results. When I used it to make a phone call, I could barely hear my hubby until I checked the volume level on my iPhone. Once I increased the audio level for that, then I could increase or decrease on the communicator. I could also turn off the ability for anyone on the other end to hear me. I liked that I could use my controller (only the new model) without any other attachments. It will not plug into the first gen Xbox one controllers.

title: Not a fan at all!
text:
I see a ton of positive reviews, and that might be people coming from WoW. To me, this is nothing but a cookie cutter future WoW, with some active combat.

The game is fun the first few levels, then becomes a race to 50, which is very easy. Took me around 30 hours of playing time to reach 50, with the typical push button get banana quest.

I also don't usually beat games up, to each their own, but this game isn't that good once you have played it for a few days. PvP is a joke, if someone runs around in circles you are screwed (Had lvl 50 Engineer). Maybe I am getting to old to keep up with the younger players, but the combat system felt silly to me. Only having 8 actions to choose from sucked too, as 2 of mine where taken up with bots, one was for the power booster, and one for spam electricity.

I have played every MMO out there, and this one was just a boring game to me. I am sure some will love it, but this is just not for me. I am gonna go check out Arch Age.

title: Finally...
text:
Finally I got burned with Call of Duty: Black Ops. At the time of purchase there was no reference or opinion to this game and since I had so far been able to get some awesome titles for the PS3 (Red Redemption, Uncharted, God of War, Little Big Planet, Batman Arkham Asylum, etc.) I thought I could not do wrong. Well, I could and I did when I purchased this very annoying and certainly way below my expectations title. So much, in fact, that after playing it for 1 hour I want nothing more to do with this let down game. It freezes, its movement is tedious and all you do is blast away while screams and total chaos unfold. This is the first and last time I will venture on my own, without the valuable opinion of those who play and know, and purchase a video game for the PS3 or any other system. Now I am burdened with the task of unloading this CIA fiasco before it damages my PS3 console, who so far has delighted us every playing hour. Will not risk the abuse this game puts it through, it is not worth it.
Also, this first person angle where all you see is the front of your weapon or knife or whatever crap you are holding is seriously two steps back from the more developed titles I have been enjoying. You are supposed to follow follow, not really knowing where you are going and how you got there. Beware of this shooter! All it's going to do is shoot your day down and is not worth it. 1 sad star!

title: Great Mouse!
text:
Disclaimer: I was given one of these to review by the company to give my honest opinion of the product.

This mouse is great!
It is weighted better than their other gaming mouse. It is well built and well balanced. Very ergonomic and comfortably fits in my hand.
It has many buttons to set to use with gaming and is functional on a pc and works with games. Remember to use the software given.
The color can be changed from blue. Its DPI is fast (faster than most mice and trackpads I have used through the years.
This mouse works well on both Mac and WIN PC as a basic mouse.
It is an excellent mouse for gaming on the WIN PC only.

Physical features of the device and accessories:
- Braided Cable
- Constructed of metal and durable comfort plastic
- Has a case for weights
- Ergonomic design
- wheel made of durable rubber
- great packaging

The only downsides are 1) they use the small CDROMs for the software (but a plus is they have it available online.) 2) they do not have driver support for the Mac and there is no sufficient third party driver that would recognize all the buttons.

I hope that with future renditions the company considers making a Mac driver as gaming is improving on the Mac and a sturdy well built mouse like this would do wonders to improve the gaming on the MAC OS X.

title: Seriously, get this one...
text:
My fiance and I just got a Switch and we wanted the screen protected, so we went with some “officially licensed” garbage from Best Buy for $8. As soon as I put it on, there were bubbles all over and two ridiculous smudges that seemed to have appeared out of nowhere (and I know I didn’t cause them). I immediately afterwards put an order in for this product. It only took two days because of Prime and arrived in perfect condition.

I put up pics of both the Best Buy one which brought only one protector, a wipe, a crappy cheap cloth, and a thing for bubbles (barely worked) and the Cellularize one which brought two protectors, two wipes, two nicer cloths, two things for bubbles (which I only had a couple very tiny ones so not a big deal), and two sticky sheets in case anything got stuck to the adhesive side of the protector.

The quality between the two products is immediately noticable, especially when you feel the protectors. I feel like the Best Buy one was plastic. No joke it could bend like crazy. If you do that with tempered glass (what an actual screen protector SHOULD be) then it will shatter after force is applied. Anyways, this one feels SO nice and heavy duty. It was easy to apply and is VERY clear with perfect cutouts for the little areas that need them.

I highly recommend this to anyone thinking about switching screen protectors or buying a new one. I mean $6 for two quality pieces. You just can’t beat this. My ONLY minor complaint is that they advertise it as “bubble-free” but that’s not accurate. However, if you know what you’re doing, it takes seconds to get rid of them. If you have trouble using the bubble-removing thing, just gently and slowly lift the corner nearest the bubble and reapply which will make it disappear.

title: Full of rages & very challenging!
text:
I wouldn't call myself a hardcore gamer (due to lots of work and energetic ferrets), but I am quite experienced and it's my passion and life. I played the original DK Country and good god it really requires patience and fast puzzle solving skills. This version is just as tough. Just when you come across a level and think after finishing it, "god, what kind of douchery was that..." The very next level will be ten times harder (not all the time, but very often).

This game will make you rage. I don't care if you're the most experienced gamer in the world- there's never gonna be any gamer that says they beat every level without dying at least once. I died maybe 40 times on one level alone. I almost broke my Wii but I chilled and eventually beat it. It is super challenging and I highly recommend this game to anyone who is tired of playing intense RPG or FPS games. Trust me you'll be in for a treat. Just don't kill your stuff while playing.

5/5 for a challenge which games these days lack, cute sound FX, nice graphics, easy game controls, and fun puzzles.

Long live DK!

There are some downloads coming later this year I think, multiplayer or something, and more trials.

If you like other versions of the game, or have never played before, this is the game to get.

title: Do not buy this game until it is patched again. Still broken as of 7/11/15
text:
I love this game on PC, it is great! You team up with people and pull off heists, so very fun. I had it on the 360 but it never got all the DLC or updates that the PC did, so when I saw it was coming out for the Xbone with all the maps included I had to get it. That was a mistake.

There are some issues with the voice chat, but that can be worked around by being in an XBL party and chatting there. When you try and pick your heist online, in game it's called Crime.net, the game locks up for few moments every 10-15 seconds seconds, but that is more of an annoyance then anything. The real issue is trying to join games online: you can't. When you go to Crime.net and see a game that someone is in that you want to join, you select it then on the next screen you can join it. If you try and join, it locks up for a few seconds then boots you back to the main Crime.net screen with an error message stating you can't join the game.

You can't play with people online.

You can start a game and invite people, and be invited by others, but if you have no friends with the game or none are online when you are, you will not be able to play with others.

There is a single player game of course, but you only get 2 AI players and they can do nothing except shoot and be shot. So good luck hauling bags of jewels to the escape van, it's all on you.

If the game worked it would probably get 5 stars from me. The state it is in now, it gets 1.

Oh, and as of this review it's been out in the US for about a week and there is still no patch. It was also released in the UK even earlier and there is still no patch. The previous console versions were never updated and never got the DLC that they promised players, which makes me wonder if they are going to do the same for current gen consoles now. Take the money and run? I hope not; my fingers are crossed that the game gets fixed.

I will update my review if things change.

*** UPDATE***

The game was patched! Finally! Yes! It no longer freezes when you try and join games online. Well, it doesn't freeze every few seconds on the Crime.net screen anymore. It still freezes when you select a job and try to join a game, and it still won't let you join any games.

I added a star for effort to my rating.

text:

Of course, when I try and take it off myself it doesn't ever want to and I have to work for it. Perhaps there is some simple way to do it and I am missing it.

I am never able to hit the power button with this on my 3ds, I have to use the stylus and that just means it will get worn out faster.

Because of these things I am taking off one star.

title: This game was wicked fun, especially with 2 players.
text:
It's less a game and more of an interactive movie, you can't really lose but you can change how the story goes. The graphics are great, the gameplay is fun and the sound is very good.

When I got the game, I popped it in to the PS3 and after an update was at the main menu. I went through the options and stuff, and found out there could be two players. My daughter quickly grabbed a controller and decided to play as the "spirit".

I played as the main character, doing things like walking around and beating people up. She played as the ghost or "spirit" Aiden(?) and could move stuff and do other supernatural things. Basically you switch between the two characters to get things done, CIA spy stuff or teen "Carrie" stuff, or even saving homeless people stuff. She got really mad when I wouldn't do what she wanted me to do, but I told her I play like I want and she plays like she wants.

As Aiden she can be mean and vengeful or helpful and peaceful. Once we finish the game we will have to switch parts, I want to try being a ghost and totally poltergeist that party of rowdy teens!

If there was more gameplay and less interactive movie, I would have given 5 stars. It's major funage, and even better with a friend (or relative). It's mostly like Heavy Rain; press a direction or hit a button fast. Sometimes I didn't know which direction to press in a fight, it was confusing a little, but I couldn't "die" so it was all good (after some practice I got better, but the fight sequences could have been a little more clear).

So if you are looking for a good story (told out of sequence, yeah for nonlinear) and like interactive movies, this is the game for you. And it's cheap.

And buy "Heavy Rain" too! It's also wicked fun, more so with the PS3 Move.

title: Worth every penny
text:
By far the best version of the previous 2 releases.

Battery: this seems to be a plaguing issue with the previous versions. The battery indicator on the base station eliminates the guessing game of your battery capacity. And the fact that you can put the headset down and walk away for a few minutes. The headset will power off or go into idle mode until you pick it up again.

Setup: It's plug and play. It's paired up with your PS4 once it goes into the base station

Quality: Outside material seems to be the same as the 2nd gen model. Their is a $50 mod kit available if you want to get leather ear pads. This is probably the only fault of the product. For $300, I would expect the leather ear pads to be included

Audio quality: This is where the value comes in. In the 1st and 2nd gen models. When placing a FPS, the bass and sounds get too distorted at times. Almost like it can't handle it. I set the EQ setting to Pro (option 3) and played it really loud. Sound quality didn't skip a beat

Ease of use: Previous models required the mixamp to be plugged in for a firmware update. The base station can be plugged in directly into your computer. Along with a software download so that you can manage the sound from a user friendly interface. Adjusting sound quality or using the preset options. You will always have the latest firmware update. I've had issues with the 2nd gen model on this issue, and it seems like they solved it

Price: Yes it's pricey. You can get some other headsets that are considered premium for half the cost. The strength in Astro is the comfort and quality. After a few hours of gaming or long raids. You'll tend to feel the discomfort in some headsets.

If you have the money to spend. Go for it. You won't be disappointed. This comes with a 1 year manufacturers warranty. If you can get an extended warranty through Bestbuy. I would do so in a heart beat. Playing this over the course of 2 years at maximum output might have its wear and tear issue.

I picked up a pair of these when I needed to send my trusty G930 headset in to get exchanged. My wife and I work back-to-back in a home office, and she is on the phone a lot, so I was looking for a headset that was comfortable to wear all day and would effectively isolate noise so that her voice wouldn't carry into my mic for my calls (mic noise cancellation), and also would not intrude on my music when I wasn't on a call (headphone noise cancellation).

The box advertised all of this, so I went ahead and got it.

PROS:
- It is indeed comfortable for all-day wear.
- Good audio quality (better bass than the G930, but otherwise equal quality, IMO)
- Being able to retract the mic is nice.
- The 3.5mm plugs mean I can use these with portable music players when I travel.

CONS:
- Microphone quality is terrible.
- Microphone mute switch doesn't work 100%.
- No advertised "30dB noise isolation" in the headphones.

On my very first call, I kept being asked whether I was in a busy office or a train station or something because the microphone was picking up -everything-. I tried to lower the volume, but it was impossible to find a setting where the other party could hear me without hearing everything else in the room (not to mention noise / static galore).

I also tried to use the in-line mic mute switch, but it apparently didn't do a full job - it just muted the volume of the microphone by about 90%, so you could still hear things through the mic at a very low volume (confirmed by listening to the audio stream on loopback).

These two things meant that I had to keep going to the softphone's mute button and un-muting myself to talk, then re-muting afterwards. Very inconvenient.

As far as the "30dB noise isolation" goes, I might as well not be wearing the headphones. I can hear everything outside the headphones extremely clearly, even my wife typing on the keyboard (it's a soft-touch keyboard, too, so the raw sound is not that loud). I have no idea who thought that there was ANY noise isolation whatsoever.

These will be going back to the store as soon as I get my G930 back.

title: Awesome Keyboard for Anything!
text:
[[VIDEOID:fde036749dec9bb4a99e2fc8728e7f60]] Now this comes down to personal preference of the type of keyboard you like. If you like a quite soft touch keyboard then I wouldn't purchase this one. This is a great mechanical keyboard that has so many different and unique options you'll be playing with different configurations for a while. I love this style keyboard myself and wouldn't trade it for anything. I had been looking for a good mechanical keyboard at a good price and this one was perfect. This has the look and feel of a full mechanical keyboard with the benefits of a membrane keyboard. I didn't realize this until I had gotten it and used it a while. After realizing it I saw the uniqueness of it and how well it worked. I honestly couldn't notice until I removed a key.

I love the fact that it is heavy and feels solid. The edges are sharp and can cut you if you aren't careful so this certainly isn't for younger kids. I sincerely believe that this keyboard will outlast the next three computers. It really seems that well built and sturdy. I'm don't find the mobile phone holder useful but that's probably because I don't really use my phone in landscape mode and it has to sit on something solid to remain in portrait mode while resting there. This is an amazing keyboard for the price and feels exactly the way I like a keyboard to feel.

Just remember it feels much more like a full mechanical keyboard then a membrane one so if that is what you are looking for then this is defiantly it and you won't be disappointed!

I have to say that there is no way you could be disappointed with this mouse for the money.  It's a bit light for my personal taste because I like a little heft but it seems that most people now-a-days prefer lighter products.  I really expected to be sending this back but instead it is currently running on one my systems.  I haven't tried it on an Xbox One or PS/4 yet, but I don't see why it wouldn't work.  To be completely honest the USB C adapter that comes with it is worth the price of the mouse.  I sincerely hope everyone enjoys this value priced gaming mouse as much as I do. title: Still a Great Game All These Years Later!
text: I have been playing this game every year since it came out in 2007, 2K Sports have always had the edge over EA Sports when it came to basketball games. The fluid motions, ease of playing and overall enjoyment is great. For those who are unaware, College Basketball games have stopped being made since 2009, the last of which was NCAA Basketball 10 by EA Sports. While the EA game has an ESPN feel, the game seems to lack the heart and excitement that College Hoops gives you. The legacy mode in College Hoops cannot be beat, everything is controllable from recruiting, training, schedules, even creating your own chants. Oh and of course the weekly NCAA show, (the same thing EA still has yet to put into any of its games). The fact that NCAA Basketball 10 is 2 years older than the last College Hoops game is the only reason people are paying 3x the amount than Hoops 2K8. If you are stuck on the fence between the 2, choose 2K8, you will not regret your decision.

title: A Must For Every WWE Fan Old & New
text: So i was able to get this when Amazon had it on sale for $30. At that price i was sure not to be let down had i not liked the game, like WWE 12, which for some reason came off as too big of a change with very little payoff. The main selling point to me, much like many others was the Attitude Era, which hands down is the greatest feature ever put into a WWE game. Being able to relive all the moments i remember from my childhood, the classic matches, incredible moments, and all the characters in between. (Not to mention they show stock video footage as you progress, heck they show more in this game than the WWE Attitude Era dvd recently put out). There were times when i was jumping up and down with excitement like i did all those years ago, the same excitement i would get from playing old classic THQ games No Mercy and Wrestlemainia 2000 for Nintendo 64. The entrances are great, still some issues with commentary and crowd noise, maybe not as noticeable without surround sound, but a minor flaw to say the least. The roster is impressive, but with some of the characters missing, does disappoint, the DLC packs do help a bit with adding a few of the up and coming talent but with THQ going bankrupt dont expect to see any additional content to be released. Having said that creating superstars or using the online community to download other created superstars is very impressive to give you those must have superstars not in the game. For what i paid i am very happy with the game, and is a great step up for WWE 12. Dont know what will happen going forward, but this was a game to put THQ out on a high note.

title: My son would play this every day if I let him.
text:
For play, you need the basic Wii, the controller that usually comes with it, and you need to have the numchuck control (it holds the force and is how you change characters. You'll also use this for boxing games on the Wii).

All the characters are from Lego mini figures, and the ships, levers, and buildings are made of legos, so none of the violence is remotely real- it's all done with toys.=)

My son says:
Every single Star Wars episode from 1 to 6 is represented. From episode one you can play an extremely simple game called negotiations, you go through corridors full of dangers, trying to survive multiple droids in order to get to a droid transportation ship to hi-jack. There are podraces. The last level for episode three is called Darth Vader, you're Darth Vader, first crossing a fragile floor, trying to avoid the lava below, fighting Anakim, and multiple droids. There's a hoth battle (from episode five), you're in Luke's ship and you have to bomb your way through multiple doors and avoid the spydroids.

Wii is more fun than game cube because in levels like the podrace you can actually know what you're doing and be going extremely fast.

This game works better when you use the controls on the Wii remote, pressing the buttons gives you more control over your moves than swinging. For instance, you press A two times you'll double jump in the air. If you press B in midair, then you'll be kneeling in the air on the way down and can destroy almost anything. You can react faster with the Wii games than with game cube, too.

I like it because, unlike other computer games, my son mostly plays it standing up and moving around.

title: For work, nothing beats this
text:
I waited to purchase a keyboard, wanting the right deal, and this one is definitely it! Rosewill used to be a bit bargain basement, but they've really stepped it up recently, and this is a great, low-cost option to get some real Cherry MX switches under your fingertips for cheap.

I was originally looking at [[ASIN:B00S5E4KH2 Rosewill Mechanical Gaming Keyboard with Cherry MX Blue Switches (RK-9000V2)]], which I am sure is a great keyboard, but I did notice that the reviews stated that the cord left something to be desired. title: Perfect. Holds Switch, Games, Cables. You won't be disappointed.
text:
I did a lot of research before buying a Nintendo Switch case. Reading reviews here on Amazon, searching for case buying guides on Google and even reading a few long and opinionated threads on reddit. I then decided on the Butterfox case. Before I tell you my opinion, here's what was my requirements.

- sturdy, solid case, able to protect from bumps
- handle, so it was easy to carry
- storage for cables, joy-con straps (not the joy con grip, just the straps)
- storage for games
- no pesky elastic straps that might rub against the console

Happy to say the case delivers on all accounts. Starting with storage, it has enough room for a USB-C cable (6ft Anker cable) and the joy con straps. It's probably too tight for a charging plug as well, but I carry an Anker 5 port charger separately anyway.The cables all sit in a zip pouch.

There's a center flip part that can hold your switch games. It holds a lot. I haven't counted how many, but more than enough.

The switch sits snugly in the case. Not too tight but tight enough to hold it snug. So it's easy to get in and out. Butterfox were smart and there's a handy piece of material to make it easy to lift your switch out. The game card flap then velcro's down to provide extra protection of the screen and hold the switch in place.

All of the zippers are smooth. There's no weird plastic smell. Overall, very impressed.

Negatives
None. Wish I had purchased one with color zips. I purchase the entire black one. Which is great, but I wish I had some color to make it stand out in the bottom of my bag.
