title: Quality sound and an impressive Mic
text:
I used my Sennheiser Game One's as a comparison. In their heyday they were in the $250 range (although they are half that price now, oh technology why do you hate my wallet so much). Anyway, I figured they would be the best set on hand I could test against. Both sets were tested on my system with a dedicated sound card (soundblaster Z) and on my hubby's system without a dedicated sound card. I tested for PC use only, so if these are for an xbox keep that in mind.

Need for dedicated soundcard: First off, while the Senn's require the soundcard to pull enough power and not crash my computer, the Astros proAmp thing either compensated enough to not need one, or this headset is fine without a sound card. Either way, I did NOT need a dedicated soundcard for the Astro's.

Overall sound quality: ok the Senn's sound slightly richer. Not above and beyond but the sound seems "warmer" and more immersive. I'm not saying the Astro's were bad, they passed all the sound tests I ran with flying colors, pulling in a wide range of super low bass and super annoying high frequency. I'm just partial to the Senn's, but the Astros were excellent in their own right.

Microphone: Ok this is where the Astros shined. They isolated the noise better, voice was much clearer, and they triggered Discords auto-enable flawlessly. My Senn's often clip the start of my words even on the highest sensitivity.

Muting: Going with the Senn's on this one, flip mic to mute is just awesome. Astros have an inline mute, that you slide. When muted the LED lights on the proAmp turns red which is a nice visual to know you are muted. Flip up mic is more of a preference, but I’ve heard enough drama in discord from people forgetting to mute than it’s a life choice more than a preference :P

Fifth, comfort: Senn's win this one with a caveat, they are a lot warmer. All that super cush comes at a price, they make your head hot after a bit. The Astros weren't as squishy soft, but they are better ventilated and lighter.

Conclusion: Compared to my Senn’s I say they average out to being equals. Sound is great, the mic is amazing, and all the replaceable parts on the Astros incase they wear out make these a really great set. The only real negative is the instruction sheet. IT IS AWFUL. Seriously they wrote it in like 3pt font in light grey. They have a diagram on one side that is rather pointless and HUGE, then the actual instructions on the back are super tiny. If I were writing a review for instructions alone this would be 2 star review. Thankfully its for the headset, so I’m only dinging them one star for the terrible instructions, lack of cush on the padding, and the price point. For $250 gaming headset you gotta hit all the categories out of the park. These did well, but my Senn’s are now half that price and comparable in performance.

title: High quality; good value
text:
There are two things I especially love about this headset. The first is the weight. It's extremely light, so it is a comfortable headset to wear for a long gaming session, or a long session of teleconferences, or maybe a bit of both.

The second thing is the sound quality. At the price point, I didn't expect much and I was pleasantly surprised. These stand on par with some of the more expensive headsets I've tried. I wouldn't say they're the best -- they aren't going to deliver the quality of a $200 Turtle Beach for example -- but they're good enough for most purposes, excellent for gaming, and a good balance of cost and quality.

The headset plugs into a PS4/XBox One Controller (or a Nintendo Switch or a cell phone or anything else with a single jack for headphone and mike) and it comes with an adapter to split the input and output so you can plug it into the PC, and the cord is suitably long for both purposes. The microphone control is on the wire. The headphones fold for easy storage.

You can sneak up on guards and take them out. Or you can sneak past them. You can hack machines to lead them into traps. You can hack phones or traffic lights or whatever for distraction. There are a lot of options.

I found the story compelling enough for a game (or even a movie; it was really good) and the gameplay especially excellent.

I haven't had much experience with the multiplayer, but that's not really my thing anyway. As a single player experience, it makes up for the lack of an AC game this year.

Loved it.

title: Very good game
text:
I know this game has its detractors, but I am enjoying it quite a lot. Aside for the near constant presence of rats the size of cats (yes, we have them; no they don't run down the streets in anything like those numbers but rather haunt subway tracks) it's a perfect rendering of New York. There have been many times I don't need the overhead map to show where I am to go. I know the neighborhood. I've been there.

It is absolutely a tactical shooter, and you will find it much easier to defeat the opponents if you think in terms of the best tactical approach rather than charge in recklessly (indeed, it's nearly impossibly to finish any of the missions by charging in recklessly). You need to keep cover, keep a positional advantage, and not get surrounded. You need to use the terrain to your advantage.

It's good for single player and especially good if you can get online with a friend or friends and play together. The story is engaging, the gameplay is strong.

You can do hunter/gatherer missions, getting data and supplies to build up your base. You can do shoot the enemy missions (rescue hostages; drive off the bad guys). You can go head to head with other players in the dark zone. Whatever suits your whim of the moment. It's a rich and varied experience.

title: Clumsy interface and nothing seems to work
text:
I so wanted to like this system. It's a mess.

First off, the interface is clunky as all get up. I could not figure out how to get to what I was trying to click on. For the Crunchroll app (one of the few video streaming apps that is supported, more on that later) I had to use the arrow on the remote control (not included, and a useful accessory) to get to the search button. The arrow is a button that does not look like a button on that controller. You make the cursor go away by pushing any other button. The shift is like the shift on a keyboard, not a phone. You need to hold it down to get a capital letter. With a Lego Yoda game, I could find no way to click on the choice between dark and light side. Some of the games work, but it's hit or miss.

I set the system default language to English, so the games kept defaulting to French. For the farming game that comes with it, I could not see how to swap it before the tutorial began.

I am using an Ethernet connection so the system keeps saying it won't download until I connect to WiFi (clearly it checks for WiFi and then assumes I'm on a cellular plan). This gets annoying.

The main feature is its ability to stream GameFly games, but the game lists are paltry. The plans are by genre, so if you want say family games and action games, you need two subscriptions. Not that there is much to recommend any of the packages. Most have few games, and only one or two popular ones per subscription.

Forget streaming video. Crunchyroll, Crackle, and HBO Go were supported, and YouTube of course, but no Hulu, no Vudu, no Netflix, no Amazon Video. The pickings are sparse. Crunchyroll did not stream cleanly, but rather had an odd border around the video.

That leaves the ability to stream pc games to the device, in the odd situation that your PC does not have an HDMI port (a splitter will let you put out to TV and monitor both). I found that of dubious value since my PC already goes to the TV at need.

I love the idea of an Android gaming platform. I loved the Ouya. This is a sad entry.

title: Good first gaming mouse, especially for its ease of use
text:
I'm using this on PC, and can't speak to how it works on a Mac, but for PC it's excellent in its price category.

The DPI buttons are intuitive. The big one makes it more sensitive. The little one makes it more precise. There are three settings, typical of most gaming mice, the most sensitive flies around the screen for strafing, etc. The middle one is basically your typical day to day mouse sensitivity. The least sensitive is for precision, sniping the zombie on the building across the way, that sort of thing. I like how intuitive and accessible these are, for rapid switching on the fly.

I find the low setting also works well for software developers if you need finer control when laying design elements for a UI in a tool like Visual Studio. On that score, a friend and fellow developer said the mouse "felt weird". I'm used to gaming mice, so it seemed fine to me. There is a little thumb rest (this is very much meant for a right handed person) and above that rest are the forward/backward buttons. The mouse is deep enough not to his them unintentionally during intense play.

The mode button on the bottom switches modes, which out of the box means color schemes. I didn't customize the buttons. I felt no need. Lights are on the scroll wheel, the sides, and the logo on the back. The right and left buttons show no separation to show that they are buttons making for a sleek design. The ample red and black cable echoes the colors on the mouse.

If I had any complaint, it's that the forward button is textured and the back isn't. Given how they are positioned, it's not for any type of tactile clarity, so I don't see why they don't match. It's a small point.

For someone looking to get into gaming mice, this is a great intro unit, both in terms of ease of use and in terms of price point. I received a sample in exchange for an honest review.

title: Good for marathon gaming sessions
text:
It clips neatly and easily onto the DualShock 4. I have charged it from both the PS4 and the PlayStation TV with no issues. It's not hard to move it from controller to controller if you have multiple systems. If it's not pushed in properly, it just falls off, so no issue of accidentally not seating it properly.

I tend towards marathon gaming sessions now and again, and one of the most annoying things is when the controller dies a few hours in. With this, I've managed to take it to seven hours total (controller plus extended battery power bank both at full) and it still had some charge at the end. That's 2 - 3 hours above what the controller alone could do.

It would be nice if it had a separate charge indicator, but that's the only nit I could pick. I like it.

title: Lightweight and responsive
text:
It's hard not to compare this to the Elite.

On the plus side, it is lighter and feels better in my hands. It's easy to configure the buttons and the triggers are very responsive.

On the minus side, the components don't interchange, the buttons on the back are smaller, and might be a bit too small. The most important consideration is that this is strictly a wired controller. If you are using it on PC, great, and it does work nicely on Windows 10. If you are using it on the XBox One, the cord is on the short side. You will want a USB extension cable.

Overall, I love the feel of it, and I adore the responsiveness.

title: Mindblowing!
text:
I've always liked racing games. I can't say they were ever my favorite genre, but I enjoy them. I played Forza 4 on the 360 with an economy wheel and had a splendid time of it.

Playing Forza 6 with this was an entirely different experience. My hands were shaking; my heart was pounding. It has been a long time since a game did that to me. The wheel fights like a real wheel. You go into a skid and you need to struggle that wheel to go where you want. It's not so much strength as skills, and it's amazing. If you release the wheel slightly, like you might in a real car after a turn, it rights itself exactly as a real car will. It turns pretty much as much as a real car's wheel will in any direction.

You can, of course, attach it to a table or something like -- it connects with a small clamp tightened by two knobs on top that look like buttons (twist them if you're having trouble and the clamps with slowly descend or ascend) but if you're going to go with a wheel of this quality, you may want to go all the way with a wheel stand. It makes a difference in comfort and stability. On the folding table I tried the table tipped, the whole thing shifted around, and it was bad. With even an entry level stand, so long as it has a board to clamp this too, it is perfect.

If you want the most intense racing experience possible, you want this wheel. There are cheaper out there, but the quality difference is severe.

title: Go buy Rock Band instead
text:
You need to pair the guitars to the USB dongles. Unlike say Rock Band where they are just Bluetooth. If you buy the two pack, good luck remembering which dongle goes to which guitar.

You can't buy songs, to play over and over, it's more a jute box situation where you buy plays. The good news is you can earn them in game. The bad news is you have to play whatever it throws at you to get them.

The controller disconnects repeatedly, so the game puts up an error message, but the notes keep coming. New batteries didn't help. Clear line to the dongle didn't help. The thing just doesn't work.

You can't calibrate the game manually. At best you can let it sort of figure it out on its own. At best, it suggests putting the TV in game mode. Calibration was a well-established technique back in Gen 7.

title: Awesome wheel
text:
This is pretty much the sweet spot between a basic wheel that lacks force feedback and a top of the line wheel that costs more than a console. It clamps to the table (and do clamp it, or it'll go bouncing around if you crash into something).

It is fully wired. You need to plug it in for power, and the cord is pretty short so you may want an extension cord, and you plug the wheel into the USB port on the PS3 or PS4, so you may need a USB extender if you're far from the TV. I'm playing at about 80 inches from the TV with no issue, but that's close to the limit.

The force feedback is adjustable, at least if you're playing Project Cars, and it's a good idea to flip through the options to find the one that's right for you. It emulates a semi-automatic car with gear shifting paddles behind the wheel. Project Cars at least responds to that. Since I've never driven anything but an automatic, I'm basically flapping them around trying to get a sense of what they do. The wheel is comfortable to hold and turns easily enough, but with a little more resistance than a real car. The pedals are big, close enough to the size of the pedals in a real car as to make it hard to notice the difference. If you are playing on a hardwood floor the pedals will slip around. Get a welcome mat to put under them when they are in use and they will stay put, this assuming you are attaching the wheel to the table and not going all the way with a frame setup. The pedals are responsive and adjustable. In the default configuration the break offers more resistance than the gas.

The PS3/PS4 switcher is fairly hidden in the front behind the wheel, as it should be given you will be using that switch least of all. You have full controls for both, including a dpad, options, share, and the triggers (but not the bumpers L1 and R1 that I've seen) right on the wheel. Project Cars (can you guess my favorite PS4 racing game?) recognized it with no configuration required.

Overall this is a lot easier and a lot more fun than racing with the controller. I'm having a blast. Now if only I could stop crashing into the walls.

Awesome wheel This is pretty much the sweet spot between a basic wheel that lacks force feedback and a top of the line wheel that costs more than a console. It clamps to the table (and do clamp it, or it'll go bouncing around if you crash into something).

It is fully wired. You need to plug it in for power, and the cord is pretty short so you may want an extension cord, and you plug the wheel into the USB port on the PS3 or PS4, so you may need a USB extender if you're far from the TV. I'm playing at about 80 inches from the TV with no issue, but that's close to the limit.

The force feedback is adjustable, at least if you're playing Project Cars, and it's a good idea to flip through the options to find the one that's right for you. It emulates a semi-automatic car with gear shifting paddles behind the wheel. Project Cars at least responds to that. Since I've never driven anything but an automatic, I'm basically flapping them around trying to get a sense of what they do. The wheel is comfortable to hold and turns easily enough, but with a little more resistance than a real car. The pedals are big, close enough to the size of the pedals in a real car as to make it hard to notice the difference. If you are playing on a hardwood floor the pedals will slip around. Get a welcome mat to put under them when they are in use and they will stay put, this assuming you are attaching the wheel to the table and not going all the way with a frame setup. The pedals are responsive and adjustable. In the default configuration the break offers more resistance than the gas.

The PS3/PS4 switcher is fairly hidden in the front behind the wheel, as it should be given you will be using that switch least of all. You have full controls for both, including a dpad, options, share, and the triggers (but not the bumpers L1 and R1 that I've seen) right on the wheel. Project Cars (can you guess my favorite PS4 racing game?) recognized it with no configuration required.

Overall this is a lot easier and a lot more fun than racing with the controller. I'm having a blast. Now if only I could stop crashing into the walls.

title: No PS3, meh for PC, awesome for PS4.
text:
As has been pointed out, they do not work on the PS3 as advertised. They are for the PS4 only. There is a separate audio cable that goes into microphone in and headphones out of a PC. When I use that, I get sound in one ear only, so not recommended for that purpose. I'm dinging it one star for lack of PS3 support.

They are very comfortable, and both the headset and sound quality are excellent. Plug them in and the system immediately recognizes them. I needed to go into the accessories menu and lower the volume, because the mike pickup is very good, and I'm excessively soft spoken, The poor guy at the deli has to practically lean over the counter to hear me. These were popping into the red zone for me. They could easily pick up someone calling in from the next room.

The cable is very long, enough so that you can put the controller off to the side without taking off the headset. This would be useful for a game like Final Fantasy: A Realm Reborn. You could talk to your friends, while using a keyboard for emotes and the like (is mine the only group that likes dancing in the dungeon?) The microphone too is fairly long and easy to properly position.

They work well with portable electronics. I used them on an iPad Air and got stereo sound of respectable quality. Pretty much anything with a 3.5mm jack can use them as headphones.

The mute button is easily reached, and one of the main reasons I wanted these. I'm kind of tired of running co-op missions in Assassin's Creed Unity where the other player doesn't have a headset. So they can hear everything on my end, and I can hear nothing on theirs, and I figure I'm probably annoying them with the meow of a cat interfering with the in game sound. So the ability to rapidly mute and unmute depending on who I get paired with matters a lot. It's really easy with these, even without taking the headset off. Just slide the only button (and a fairly large one) on the left earpiece and you're either chatting or silent. Easy.

They take no adjustment, but they need none. They kind of adjust themselves. They don't get sweaty, even in July.

title: Fabulous headset.
text:
The sound quality is remarkable. It levels the volume a bit, which I like. I've played a few games (cough AC Unity cough) where the background noise can be loud and then the dialog drops inexplicably. This makes it all a bit more even. The tonal range, bass to treble, is quite good. I noticed no distortion. You can hear yourself in the headset, which I find important. It is very good at blocking out external sound, so don't expect to hear someone calling to you from the next room.

One thing to keep in mind, the microphone can sort of kind of go in backwards, and it's nasty uncomfortable if you do that. It should be set up such that the mike is on the left hand side. I have no idea if it works the other way. I didn't want to deal with that. I do know it seems to click in and it stays. I wouldn't think it should make a difference in terms of comfort, but it does. Even when using them without the microphone, having them not be backwards makes a big difference in comfort.

I found these to be snug, but comfortable. They adjust easily. The mute button is the only button on the right front, so it is easy to access. I would have liked a visual indicator if the mike is muted, but that's a small thing. Again, remember to shut off the chat feature on the Kinect if you want to be able to speak to someone privately (or to not annoy your teammates with the blare of an air raid siren, if you're in a neighborhood like mine that has one -- no air raids, just a peaceful siren to herald in the calm of the weekend).

These charge on USB and they charge fairly quickly. An indicator light on the earpiece tells you if they are charged, and if they are on. And of course the XBox will show you on screen to whom the device is paired.

I know it's not supposed to work with a hub, but I had a spare and I needed this and a keyboard to go into the same port, so I experimented. I used http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00H0PLQHO?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00 as the hub and http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003SVSJ1K?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_search_detailpage as the keyboard and mouse. I then went into Kinect and turned off the Use Kinect for Chat feature. I tried first a Skype call (call testing service) to keep things simple, and that worked. I then tried it in game, and that worked too. I put them in the port on the side towards the front, not the back port--no choice because the back ports are used for external drives but work mentioning as that has given my trouble in the past with the keyboard and I suspect the headset would fare no better. So if you aren't getting a good signal, try that port.

I tried one more thing it's not supposed to do, and it doesn't do it. It doesn't work with the PS4. Unusual, since normally any headset with a 3.5mm connection can work with that. It will function as headphones, but it cannot detect the microphone. If you want one headset for multiple systems, this isn't it. If you want a truly excellent headset for the XBox One, this most definitely qualifies.

title: Quick, simple
text:
During the height of the hacks last winter, I was nervous about giving Microsoft or Sony my credit card number. To be fair, the one time my XBox account was hacked, Microsoft issued a refund quickly and let me keep the games purchased fraudulently (nothing I'd ever want to play, so I wish they'd have taken them off my account, but I respect it was a nice gesture). Picking up a code at Amazon and registering it on the XBox was a fast, safer way to pick up digital content at the time.

I've continued to fund my XBox account this way ever since. It may be unfair, but I trust Amazon more. Delivery is nearly instant, and registering the code is fast and easy.

title: Underrated, don't miss this fantastic game
text:
This is the true successor to Black Flag, the real Assassin's Creed of 2014.

It almost feels like Unity was where the pencil pushers focused to make sure it has everything the nex gen should, by the books, it follows all the templates, and they pretty much left the Rogue team to do what they wanted. That's how it comes off anyway.

This is perhaps the best Assassin's Creed game yet. From Black Flag, you retain sea battles, navel forts, and whaling. We see a return of building up districts by investing in renovating properties that we first encountered with Ezio. Game play is pretty much as you'd expect from this series, no major divergence from the franchise there.

The story is top rate. Shay starts as an assassin, disenfranchised perhaps, but loyal to the cause. He's a contemporary to Connor, and we see Adewale a few times in the game. Over the course of the story, he sees the unintended consequences of the assassins' actions. He sides with the Templars, not because he believes in their visions of world domination -- and the modern day storyline reminds us that they are the bad guys, this is not a good vs good scenario -- but because he wants to stop the destruction being unwittingly wrought by the assassins.

History is still the playground, and we meet some amazing historic figures, the primary one being Benjamin Franklin. We're running around the colonies during the American Revolution.

I can find no flaw with this game. I encountered no bugs. I loved the story, the characters, the gameplay, and the open world. This is a technically and artistically perfect game.

title: Pickup is weak, sound field is amazing
text:
It comes with a USB cable to update the controller. I found that odd, but convenient. I can always use extra cables. The adapter has controls to increase game sounds, increase chat sounds, mute the microphone (it lights up if the mike is muted--a very convenient feature) and it can turn up and down the volume as a whole. The audio cable is standard, so you can use it in anything else that works with a headphone. The microphone retracts well enough to be invisible if you don't know to look for it. I used it for a bit with my 3DS and it worked fine for that. The audio cable is permanently attached, and I do not like that design choice. The cable is the single most likely part to break (worse for me because my cat chews these cables, but true in general). A port with a swappable cable would increase the lifespan of these headphones, and would offer choices in terms of swapping to a longer cable, a shorter cable. A more modular design is always a better choice.

It's a good size for a female. The microphone is well places (more on that in a bit) and the headset fits well and is comfortable. It's lightweight, comfortable, and easy to wear for long gaming sessions. The padding was soft without being annoying or sweaty. The ear cups don't annoy the ears the way some can after a long while.

As I said, the microphone sits well. It sits exactly where other headsets I have used sits. For me at least, position isn't a problem. The problem is that the pickup is lacking. title: Amazing!
text:
I am in love with this console.

The graphics are amazing. I love the look of the games on this system. The sound is impeccable. We run it off a 7.1 surround system, and I've had moments where a twig will snap behind me, or a beast will roar off to the left. It is a bit more precise that I'm used to in how it handles locating sound between speakers, by firing both off but not at the same volume. I really love that.

The controller is so comfortable. I had some problems early on with the rubber coming off, but each time Sony was great about quickly replacing the controller. The audio jack on the controller means even the most basic headset can be effectively wireless for gaming. I did not think I would like the touchpad, but now I love it. It has an accelerometer, so for Infamous: Second Son, when you are using the controller like a can of spray paint, you have to turn it sideways and shake it. And the embedded speakers are such, it sounds like a can of spray paint being shaken. The PS3 controller always bothered me a little that it is too easy to inadvertently push down the left thumbpad (so it thinks you hit L3) when you are trying to run around. I've yet to encounter that problem with this one, not even doing the various rundown sections of Assassin's Creed: Black Flag.

Sharing in-game video is quick and easy. It works so well, and so fast. I didn't think I would use that, but it turns out I kind of like sharing awesome moments on Facebook. I'm very much a solo gamer, and the library for that is still very impressive.

If you have PlayStation Plus, your games are backed up online. When I upgraded the hard drive, which is ridiculously simple, I just redownloaded my games, already in progress. It picked up where it left out without a hitch.

For stability, for elegance, for performance, and most importantly, for incredible game play, I give the PS4 five stars.

title: Great for the PS4, okay for the PS3, not so good for the Vita.
text:
It has good audio prompts, like "Charging Battery", "Powering On" and "Powering Off", so you are clear on what it is doing, which is cool.

It can pair to the PS4 two ways. You can plug the Optical cable into the USB dongle, plug that into the USB port, and go fully wireless. Or you can use the enclosed audio cable plugged into the PS4 controller. Both are easy to set up. Both work.

For the PS3, you need to plug the Optical cable into the USB dongle, plug that into the USB port, and then go monkey around with the settings until it finally works. That one will work, but it is more of a pain.

For the Vita, or any other media device, it should be simple. You just plug the enclosed audio cable into the headphone jack, turn on the headphones, and you're good to go. Only after a little while it says "Automatic shutdown enabled. Press the power button to cancel." If you press the power button, it says "Automatic shutdown disabled". What it does after that is up to a coin toss. It will either tell you it's powering off and then proceed to do so, or it will stay on. I've yet to figure out the pattern. I would have assumed that I did not press the button, or that it did not register, were it not for the audio prompt that automatic shutdown was disabled. I might have blamed it on the battery if it didn't happen less than an hour after a full charge, and right before staying on for an additional 45 minutes.

It has little blue Turtle Beach logos on either side that glow red while the device is charging, blue when it is charged, and flashes blue when it is in use. I would have preferred a stable light to the flashing, or even no light to the flashing. If I can hear noise, I know it's on. The flashing is just annoying. It has separate volume controls for each earphones and microphone, and audio presets such as "bass boost", "bass and treble boost", "vocal boost" and "natural sound". I favor "vocal boost" for most games and videos, though some games sound better with "natural sound".

They are good for noise cancelling, and the sound quality is excellent. In "vocal boost" mode, videos level (the voices are not drowned out by the special effects) which I very much appreciate. Turtle Beach is known for excellent audio equipment, and the sound quality on this is flawless. Were I judging it by sound alone, it would be five stars.

The microphones attaches and detaches easily, for use as a gaming headset or just earphones. There is a mute button on the right ear, that is quite easy to get to. The buttons are spaced well enough, and distinctively enough, that they are easy to use while you wear the headset.

They are comfortable when worn on the head, but when I wear them around my neck they get grabby with my hair, which is, for me, the biggest negative.

title: Amazing sound quality
text:
It comes with the Xbox One Stereo Headset Adapter, which lets you control the volume and mute the microphone, right on the controller. It clips in on the bottom, right where the XBox One headset would go. You then plug this, or any other headset, into that. You will need to run a software update on your controller, but that's true of any headset that uses the stereo adapter.

The microphone is excellent. I'm told I sound very clear on it when using it for Skype.

The sound quality is fantastic. It is a good enough approximation of 5.1 that I can tell if something is supposed to be in front of me and to the right, or behind me and to the right. Or just flat to the right. It also sounds open. There is space in the sound, which is hard to achieve with headsets. You get that even if you are using them in an mp3 player, a tablet, a phone, whatever. I'm very impressed with these.

I find them comfortable, and I'm fussy about headsets. Many of them feel too tight and give me a headache. These feel nice.

title: Fantastic headset!
text:
These are amazing.

There is a separate control for chat volume and game volume. That feature only works on PS3, XBox One and PC. Because they can also use a standard audio jack, they are also compatible with the PS4, Wii U, Vita, and 3DS. There is an additional attachment to use them for your cell phone.

The mouthpiece is detachable, which makes them great (albeit large) for regular headphones.

These are powerfully noise cancelling, immersing you fully in the game experience. The sound quality is outstanding. They have tremendous range and seem to have some sort of built in leveling feature. If your teammate says something just as there is an explosion, the game volume reduces, the chat volume increases, and you can hear both no problem. If two players are talking, one softly, one loudly, it adjusts so that one doesn't drown out the other.

They are far more comfortable than they look, given their size. They are fully adjustable, and sit well on the head. I could wear them for hours. In fact, I may see if I can use them in place of my headset at work, because they are that comfortable and that high quality.

They have switchable side plates, either a montage of marvel characters, or Thor. The montage is very subdued, and isn't all that noticeable at a distance. The Thor plates are yummy.

title: A fabulous game that never forgets it's supposed to be fun
text:
There is way too much to love in this game.

It records you as you are dancing (or not -- you choose) and, if you have a good sense of humor, you can post it to Facebook, Twitter, or XBox Live (or not -- you choose). You can play with friends. You can play alone. You can play online. You want flexibility? This game trains it and this game has it. You want to just use it to work out? Can do.

There are beloved oldies, like YMCA. There are new hits like Roar. The oldest song I found was from 1956 -- Just a Gigolo. Flashdance, from 1984 is there is well.

title: Great for kids
text:

It features voices from the movie, and has some very cute cut scenes with Gargamel. You bounce on tomatoes like trampolines for extra height. You have to hop on a frog to defeat it. It's not the easiest game -- I'm a moderately experienced gamer and I had to fight that frog three times -- but it's not all that hard once you get the hang of it. It features a co-operative mode with Clockwork Smurf, so the kids can work together to beat the game. It's a lot of fun, with nothing to worry a parent.

The game, at least in single-player mode, can be played entirely on the GamePad, freeing up the TV. That makes the Wii U the best platform for this game, as all other elements are the same.

It's a fabulous game for children, and a guilty pleasure for those of us who grew up with the first incarnation of these little blue fellows, back in the 80s. I had a great time playing it.

title: tricky but good
text:
As has been mentioned, it is hard to connect the Kinect to this. The latch has to go all the way in to catch properly. I turned mine upside down and then sort of rocked it until it clicked. Make sure you hear that click. It took about twenty minutes. I'm dinging a star for that.

It doesn't clamp to the TV. There is no chance of it scratching the screen. It has a hinged part of the back that forms a triangle with the kinect and the tv providing other two sides. The front loops over the front of the tv for the final support. It is very easy to take on and off.

It blocks the image slightly, but only slightly. It doesn't interfere with game play but would be an itsy bit distracting when watching a movie.

I have my Tv in the corner at an angle and could not find a good place to put the Kinect on the too small TV stand. This solved the problem and gave me a little more play space as opposed to putting it in front of the TV.

Overall I am quite pleased.

title: Good chat headset
text:
For chatting, it's a nice headset. It's not going to let you listen to the game via headset (thus not inflicting it on the rest of the room). It's just for chat.

Given that purpose, it's a nice headset. It's lightweight. The cable, while enourmous, doesn't tangle. The on-wire controls are well-placed and responsive. The sound quality, and the mike, are excellent.

It plugs into the USB port on the front of the device, rather than use the XBox trick of plugging into the controller, thus the reason for the 100' cable. That will mean a wire running across the room from the device to the couch (or however you have your system arranged).

If you find it doesn't work when you first plug it in, reboot the system. For some reason, mine doesn't detect the headset if it's pluged in after the system has been turned on. I've taken to just leaving it plugged in and tucked away next to the console.

Overall, it does what it's supposed to do, and does it well.

text:

It's a good, basic case.

title: This game makes studying addicting
text:
I like most of the mini games quite well. I have a few minor nits. I wish the word search wasn't timed. I don't do those quickly in English, so I lose points when I know the word but can't find it fast enough. I don't see the point of the whack-a-mole game. The concentration game is addicting. I could play it all day long, and it's basically flash cards. The fade out writing is perfect for learning kana and kanji. So is the word card for learning to write words.

There are a few minor bugs (lesson 20 conjugates "Tabemasu" to the negative form as "Nomimasu"). Overall, it's rock solid.

Don't use this alone. It's not enough. As a supplement, however, you'd be hard pressed to find better. Any Japanese student should have this for the way it gets you to drill words and have fun doing it.

title: FINALLY! iPad Running iOS 7? This is for YOU!
text:
Let's face it, Apple has been a bit late in the game (pun intended). But what can I say, I still love the iPad.
Touted as the only wireless controller given the Apple stamp of approval, and the third iOS controller ever made, this Danish designed item packs a lot of punch in a small device.

There are two easy-to-use joysticks that really move once you get used to them, a D-pad, X, Y, A, B, and a player readout.
But here is where this item stands out, and why Apple sanctioned it, in my opinion...on the top, Trigger buttons L1 and R1 with nubbies to prevent slipping, and behind them an L2 and R2. Micro USB port on the bottom, and Bluetooth on the side.
If you are buying this as a gift, know that the above-mentioned is important because it means a greater compatibility with more complex games coming 'round the bend.

How amazing to get so much on such a small controller! And that may be a negative for some. As a female, the size is perfect and easy to transition to, but a guy with large hands might have an issue with it. Your middle fingers grip an indentation on the back, I suspect it might get crowded back there for a someone with big paws. There is a snap on piece that might make it more comfortable for men.

The charge lasts between 8 to 10 hours.

So, like anything, it takes some getting used to. But it gives another functionality to your iPad, and certainly travels well. More options than the Moga.

title: A worthy mouse with good build quality
text:
The Rat 6 mouse seems to be going for the customization market, but where it really excels is in simple build quality. The weight, smooth precision parts, and mechanical functioning of this mouse make it fell less like a peripheral and more like a piece of tactical combat gear. The buttons are well placed, it slides smoothly without catching, and the sensor does its job very well.

Perhaps my favorite feature on the Rat 7 is the small rocker switch behind the scroll wheel which can be used to raise and lower the mouse sensitivity (pointer speed) on the fly, which nearly makes the precision aim button obsolete. These aren't uncommon features on a gaming mouse these days, but they're implemented well.

I'm used to using an ambidextrous mouse and switching hands often. This mouse can be used left handed without much difficulty, but you lose access to some of the buttons and features when doing so, most notably the horizontal scroll.

I previously owned a RAT 7 and really loved it, but after a couple years it failed on me. First thing to go was the braided cable, which started to short out when parts of it were moved. I hate braided cable. Eventually, I dropped it and was surprised to find one of the buttons had broken from a short fall. In the end, if you use your mouse frequently, it's worth getting a nice one, but the really high priced ones probably aren't worth the premium.

Overall, more than worth the price difference between it and the lesser mice on the market.

title: So much fun! However, not a ton of crossover appeal to adults
text:
I'm a big fan of the Just Dance line of games, because I love getting exercise while playing. So I was excited to test out this version for kids, especially since I have a little one who will hopefully be able to play with me in a few years, and a niece who is just the right age right now.

What I loved about this is that unlike in other games in this line, the dancers on the screen are actual kids! Usually, we get some weird cartoon character with improbable fashion choices, and when I see them moving on the screen I think to myself, "of course you can do that move, you're not a person." In this game, you get to watch actual kids of different ages doing the dances, sometimes they are dressed up in silly costumes, and sometimes dressed to fit in with the theme of the video. Watching real people do the dance moves increased my enjoyment of the games dramatically, and I wish they had that option for all of the grown-up games.

The song list is fantastic for kids, and my niece was familiar with most of the songs. There were also a lot of old-fashioned favorites that I was familiar with, so we had fun together. However, most of the songs have that overly cheerful tone of most children's media, and after about a half hour, I realized that I would never voluntarily choose to play these songs over any of the songs in the grown-up games. Of course, I'm an adult, so that's to be expected, but you should be aware if you are an adult wanting to play this game, you will probably not find the song choices ones that have a lot of intergenerational appeal after the first few plays.

That said, they are great picks for kids, and the gameplay itself is a lot of fun. I'd say if your kids are young enough that you do not want them exposed to songs such as "promiscuous girl" which is an example from another Just Dance game, I would definitely choose this game. If you are comfortable with the content of the other games, I would definitely choose those, because the songs are more complex and interesting.

title: Awesome - can unlock songs while just playing normally, good song variety
text:
I'm thrilled with this latest DDR game. I own all the PS2 Dance Dance Revolution games and I love to work out a few times a week with DDR. The last few games before this one required you to go through some kind of stupid dance master mode or something to unlock songs- so I was thrilled to find that you can unlock songs, dancers, etc just by playing normally in game mode.

Two annoying things in this one:

You can't shut off the dancers

The announcer is dire - really, really bad. Luckily you can shut him up in options.

I do love that there is at least one good rap song in here, and quite a few oldies like Dub-i-Dub and Butterfly (a new remix). There's also just generally a good variety of songs. There's an interesting clubhouse reggae song that I was particularly happy to see.

I have played four nights now with a person with very different musical taste than I have, and we both enjoyed it a lot and found songs we wanted to replay each night.

I'm giving it five stars because of the simplified unlock process and the fun variety of songs. Yay for X!

title: Fun and catchy but not the best of DDR
text:
The good:
Fun, catchy songs that I immediately enjoyed playing.
Easy unlock process - you just play in free play mode to unlock songs

The bad:
Game level is a bit easier than other DDR games - I usually play standard to heavy in DDR, and with this game, I have passed every song on heavy/ expert on my first try. They were complicated enough to hold my interest, but I don't feel at all challenged here.
Only about half as many songs as a normal DDR game, graphics are clunky
The dancers, as always in DDR (I just turn them off)

For the price I found it a worthy buy - as a regular player I get bored of the same songs all the time, and so any new game that helps me mix up my workout is much appreciated. But it certainly isn't up to par with the other DDR games, much as I am enjoying playing it.

However, I could see new DDR players really enjoying this, because the music is catchy and accessible and the steps aren't too hard.

If you are a regular player, know that this is a fun diversion that you will enjoy for a good while, but isn't going to become your challenging new favorite.

title: Great songs and very little overlap with the PS2 songs
text:
I own all the DDR titles that I know of for the PS2 (Flow-Urban Dance Uprising, DDR Max 1 and 2, DDR Extreme 1 and 2, Into the Groove, Pump it Up), so I was afraid that buying a DDR title for the Xbox would have a lot of overlap in the songs offered for the PS2, but there are tons of wonderful new songs to play, and a wider range of styles. This was well worth the money.

I love how many songs have videos, and I love the quirky song choices and the range of genres. There is Istanbul (Not Constantinople) by They Might be Giants, Rock Lobster by the B-52's (with a video), Alphabet Aerobics by Blackalicious (awesome, it speeds up as the song goes so by the end you are really skipping!), Sakura (the speed changes in this one really keep me challanged), Hey Mama by the Black Eyed Peas, and Nari Narien which is fun Indian-inspired techno. The difficulties are similar to DDR Max and Extreme titles - I usually play standard to heavy and I feel like there is a lot of room to grow into this game.

My RedOctane Ignition pad with the included XBox connector works great with this game. The load times are reasonably fast, too.

This is a great addition to a full DDR library of titles.

title: Great songs, annoying "game" plot to unlock them initially
text:
This is a great game for exercising; nearly all the songs made me want to get up and move! I own DDR Max 1 and 2, Extreme 1 and 2, Flow (the rap DDR!), Pump It Up, and Into the Groove, and this is one of my most-played DDR games because of the awesome songlist.

I love how modern and danceable the songs are, and I love that so many of my old favorites are on here (Afronova here I come!). I embarassingly enough love the silly pop songs like Oops! I Did It Again, Crazy in Love, and Genie in a Bottle, and then there are others that have become favorites to dance to like Butterfly (a fast remix), Spin Spin Sugar (in which the arrows get you to turn around, which is fun!), Block Rockin' Beats, Get Busy (Shake That Thing), La Copa de la Vida (a great salsa-y track that gets me shimmying along), Pump Up the Volume, I Will Survive, Play that Funky Music, and Boom Boom Dollar.

There is a huge selection of background dancers to choose from (which I don't use, as the dancers don't really dance along with the music or keep to the beat - I prefer to just see the background animations on their own), and loads of videos.

The one thing I dislike about this game is that you have to play their rigidly-structured "game" in order to unlock songs, where you have to start dancing on a super-easy mode and pass lots of songs, while the songs you are given get harder and harder. There are some levels that have songs where the arrows come from the wrong direction or you have to hit the dance pad as many times as possible *without* hitting any arrows. This wasn't fun to me; I really wish I could have just unlocked all the songs and special additions by playing the normal old way - selecting my own level and passing new songs. It would have been fun as an additional option but I didn't care for being forced to play it to unlock all the songs.

Even with this complaint, this title is well worth adding to your DDR collection. The songs are varied and fun enough to keep you playing for a long time.

title: Years after its release, still a worthy purchase
text:
I picked this game up for some variety after starting with DDR Max2 and DDR Extreme. While DDR Max 2 is still my all-time favorite (I own Flow, Pump It Up, Into the Groove, DDR Max 1 and 2, DDR Extreme 1 and 2), this game places second in my book.

It has good variety in the difficulty levels of the songs. Some I can pass on Heavy easily after a year, and some songs I still can't pass on Standard. There are some really slow songs with a hip-hop vibe and some really fast techno ones, and songs in a whole range of styles and speeds, so whatever mood I am in, I can usually get into a good flow with this music and want to keep working out.

There is a training mode just like with DDR Max 2, where you can slow the songs down and gradually speed them up as you get better at each sequence, which is invaluable for Rhythm and Police and Exotic Ethnic, two awesome but very fast songs!

The downside to this game is that it doesn't have nonstop mode like DDR Max 2, but the game mode is structured so that you don't have to keep flipping through a ton of menus if you pass each song, so it isn't as necessary as it is with DDR Max 2.

I am grateful that DDR Max excludes the dancers as I find them distracting.

title: Great hip-hop songs and steps, but hard to read arrows
text:
I am a huge fan of DDR and hip-hop music, and this game is a great change of pace for DDR players who are tired of all the seventies hits and Japanese techno that dominates many of the other DDR games.

The arrows (dance moves) feel much more natural than on some of the other DDR games out there, and I love that on this game I almost always feel like I am dancing, rather than tapping arrows! I love the variety of songs; though most of them have a comparatively slow beat, the arrows are placed in new and different ways than I am used to, so it makes it fun as a change.

I love how the arrows that you press simultaneously are linked with a chain, so it is easy to tell when to hit those. But, the arrows are all shades of brown, so it is hard to see them against the urban-themed backgrounds, and really difficult to tell the difference between half and eighth notes. You kind of get used to it, but on Heavy mode I find myself squinting and relying on the music to figure out when to step on the more complex sequences because I can't differentiate between all the layers of brown.

This game also isn't as hard as some of the other DDR games. I play standard and heavy on the DDR Max and Extreme games, and the hardest level on this game is fun and requires focus but is doable without too much practice. I'd like another level to move up to.

The dancers are way better in this game than in the DDR Extreme games. The dancers start doing trick moves when you get a combo going, and crash to the floor from their spinning headstands if you break the combo. It is fun that they are responsive to what is going on in the game, which they aren't in DDR Extreme and Max.

Even with the complaints I have about arrow visibility and wanting more difficult levels, I enjoy this game a lot and play it often. I wouldn't buy this game as my first or only DDR game (DDR Max 2 would be my first choice!), but if you have a few games and want to mix it up, this one is really different and a lot of fun. I hope they come out with a sequel and fix those problems, because they have done a lot of things better than Konami/ Bemani and I can see their potential for a really strong hip-hop DDR game.

text: Hey, any excuse to dance and get silly with friends! I love the updates to music, so it always feel relevant and like a party. Ultimately, the game is a lot of fun and has great music, and it's a way to have fun and bond with friends and family doing something physically active. It might be one of the few contexts in which people will dance in public without feeling self-conscious, and whatever gets people interested in dance, even if it's not *exactly* like dance, is a good thing. What more can you ask for?

title: charming, simple, and fun
text:
While the special features found only in a Wii are not used much for this game (movement-based action, use of personalized charactersany Wii user knows as Miis), it is still very cute and entertaining for kids or adults. Like other sim-type games, you are able to customize environments and clothing of some characters and have the freedom to explore and interact, but the similarities mostly end there. You do not control all of the characters/are not able to switch control from one character to another, and there is some linear flow to the action. You are given a series of missions on each of a few locales; as you progress, you are allowed to explore new locales, as well as accumulate options from all current and previous locations.

The basic idea is to rebuild and fix different places and help the residents in each one. Sometimes that means finding objects, other times, talking with people to resolve conflicts. To build structures or machines, etc., you need to have certain points which can be found by toying with trees, plants, and other objects. You also need raw materials that are sometimes hidden, or other times uncovered by mining (you have to find hot spots and then use the controller like a little pick axe) or digging, as though for buried treasure.

Sometimes it is a little repetitive, but that is the nature of the genre, and all in all, the loose structure and dialogue keep things moving. It would probably be more entertaining if the characters spoke a real language, but apparently the makers wanted to save on having to do multiple voice-overs and translations, so that's a bit of a loss there, especially for some younger kids, but having dialogue is still appreciated. Also, having to figure out mechanical puzzles might be trickier for the younger crowd, it's fun having to use a little spatial reality logic to make things work, though it's not Very challenging.

Wii is definitely improving its offerings, and while this isn't the best game I've seen on the system, the charmingly rendered environment and cute characters and story make this a fun little adventure.

It's all pointless, and neither challenging nor easy. It is simply repetitive. If you want brainy games, something with a story, something with characters or any interest at all, try something else. It's not worth the money or time. Avoid similar games by this company.

title: Not as vast as Oblivion, but I was tired of that game anyway!
text:
Fable 2 is a great game and I'm glad I purchased it. To any of you who are on the fence regarding this game, here are a few points to help you make your decision:
1) I experienced zero glitches. I think patches have been loaded because I have played for 2 months and never had a problem.

2) As the title of my review states, the "world" is smaller. You don't really travel the roads from one town to another, you just "fast travel" there instead. Actually, I liked this feature because it saves time and just gets to the good stuff.

3) I really enjoyed that you don't have to rely on finding money or merchandise to sell in order to get gold for the items you need. Various jobs are available so you can control how much money you make. This is especially great at the beginning of the game.

4) It's definitely a shorter game than Oblivion, I think I logged only half as many hours in Fable 2 compared to when I beat Oblivion. What I like about this is that the ending leaves you three different options. I don't feel like "Oh, that'll take forever I can't start all over." I have already begun another game with a different character and am enjoying making different decisions this time around.

Overall, the game is definitely worth your money and I recommend it highly. I can understand other reviewers giving it low marks for lack of depth and that they beat it very quickly...but take your time and complete all the quests and enjoy the game and it won't go by too fast. The review that cracks me up is the one where someone gave it one star because they had a lo-def TV and couldn't read the text! Wow. How about giving your TV a one star review? The game is great!

CUE software is definitely a huge downside to this mouse. I wish I had gotten the Razer Naga Trinity instead if I knew this would be just as bad as their Synapse software.

title: Great game for dinosaur loving Grandson
text:
I bought this game for my 10 year old grandson. I'm the dino Grandma, having introduced him at the ripe age of 1 to the love of dinosaurs and every year I've been able to find the unusual "dino" gift to steal his heart. This game was no exception. I purchased a "gun" holder seperately and that helped a lot. He LOVES this game. And I was very impressed with the quality of the graphics and the fact that even though things get killed there isn't all the blood and guts so many of the games are like these days. Now, I'm purchasing another game for my house, so that when the kids come over, it will be here too.

My Grandson and his father are big gaming buffs. They have all the very sophistigated games like Halo and games geared toward older teens and adults. My grandson is very good at these games but I prefer that he have a fun game killing something other than people. To be told that this game was better than all the others he has played and know me means it says a lot for the game. What boy doesn't love dinosaurs and what adult male isn't the big game hunter at heart?

I don't know what exactly some of the reviewers expected, I've had all the original Jurassic Park games for our Playstation and the computer and this game beats them all. And playing it on the Wii was icing on the cake. Kudos to the makers. Kudos to Amazon for having it available for purchase.

title: In the End, I Remain Impressed
text:
Original Review:
Beautiful graphics, quirky gameplay. I'd have loved this game, but I came to a mini-game towards the end of the game that requires you to shoot 33 enemies without getting shot once. This is NOT why I play adventure type games. And there is no way to skip it, so I was deprived of the joy of finishing this lovely game.

Edited Review:
I am editing this after completing the game. I was too thick to realize that there was a way to replenish my "lives" in the mini-game I mentioned in my original review. Once I figured that out, I was able to complete the mini-game pretty easily.

In closing, I have to explain that I used to play this type of game all the time back in the heyday of "real" adventure games (like Myst). And back then, there wasn't always a walkthrough - you just puzzled it out until you figured it out. And that was half the fun. How lazy I've become! What's left of the adventure genre of games is way easier, and you can almost always skip the mini-games. So this game was very hard for me. I couldn't have finished it without a walkthrough, but that's just proof that I have become spoiled and lazy!

All in all, this is a beautiful game, beautifully designed, illustrated, and executed. They just don't make games like this anymore. If you are a fan of the old-fashioned adventure game, and particularly one with no violence (unless you count shooting at tiny red pixel bad-guys with a tiny blue pixel gun), and if you love the artwork and design in your games as much as the games themselves, Machinarium is the game for you.

title: Don't Listen To The Haters
text:
This game is extremely fun and addictive. I have played and beat all 3 campaigns which were all awesome and sometimes creepy. As a marine you have got to stay on your toes, never know when those damn Aliens or Facehuggers can pop out at you. You get a 18 round Semi auto pistol to start off with which can be a decent weapon when low on ammo but not accurate at longer ranges (as one can expect from handguns). The pulse rifle is straight from the movies and is the same model of rifle as was seen in the original Alien movie and follow up in the Prequel Aliens. This bad boy can hold 99 in each mag and is a straight shooter but be careful its rate of fire can get you into trouble if you don't stay on target. Shotgun! Love the double barrel shotgun in this game, get those pesky face huggers away from you and headshot a Alien, that will learn em! So you are surrounded by a bunch of eggs? HELLO FALMETHROWER! If you like the smartgun you will see it later on in game and it can be a life saver from the hordes! Also some decent character interaction all be it very short and brief in lvls.

Predators: You recall the first AVP movie? Ya boy, you are gonna get all those weapons my friend! The smart disc is probably my favorite weapon. Its a non lock on disc that you can throw and it will follow your laser! Get good with that and you can drop 2 or 3 aliens in one swing! Of course you will also get those huge wrist blades as well which are good for melee offense and defense. As a Predator you will also get the notorious lock on Plasma Cannon that we have all come to love! But you have limited uses so make shots count and be a true hunter. You will get 3 types of vision. Regular, Thermal (as seen in Predator 1 and 2 and AVP), and also a special vision to detect those Xenos. All said this was actually my least favorite campaign for some odd reason. Its all personal preference but it was still good fun!

Aliens: The Aliens campaign might just be my favorite with the marines a very close second. I must admit I enjoyed the creep factor and darkness of the Marine campaign a lot. But as an Alien you become a profession hunter of the dark. You can stalk and lure your prey towards you and sprint so fast they wont know what hit them. Also when you sprint you are neigh impossible to shoot when running away. Sometimes I just like teasing the Marines for a while and toy with them before killing them. BE WARNED, Aliens are probably the weakest as far as defense goes. If those Marines are packing shotguns you better have a plan. You can climb on walls ceilings, roof tops....pretty much everything, no wait scratch that you can climb on EVERYTHING. I love it! Stealth kills truly are fun! Ripping off faces, shoving that wicked tongue clamper into heads, impaling with your tail...just awesome!

Graphics: are pretty good in my book. They are not the best but far from the worst! I give the graphics an 8/10
Sound: excellent! truly the original sounds from the movies and creepy as hell at times! Keeps you on your toes. 10/10
Gameplay: Gameplay was excellent in my book. Tons of fun and challenging, super intense. Action packed but also as a Pred or Alien you needed strategy. But sometimes as an alien you could mess up on kills because of how they cling on to things. It takes a while to get used to. And I wasnt a fan of how the Preds left stealth after using certain attacks or weapons. Gameplay as a Marine was everything I could have asked for. Major creep factor to keep you on your toes, excellent action, and all the essential weapons as well from the movies. Overall the gameplay gets a 9/10.
Multiplayer: Is fun but sadly you don't see a lot of team work. I personally suck and I wont lie about it but it is still pretty fun. 8/10
Cons: This game was really short! While the lvls were decent in length you only get 5-7 lvls per campaign with the Marines having the longest campaign. I really wished we could have had more content and lvls in campaign. I killed the Predator and Alien campaigns in one sitting and wrapped things up with the Marines the very next morning.

VERDICT: 8.5 is my overall score for this game. I really think its awesome, challenging, action packed, creepy, and extremely fun. The multiplayer is fun but it does take time to get used to. The only real problem is the campaigns are too short. To remedy this I recommend trying it on hard mode. It will keep you playing much longer than easy or normal modes.

title: Total Letdown!
text: This game is NOT very good. It does NOT live up to the old RTW at all. Empires Total War is better than this garbage and that says a lot! First off the Unit/Building cards are freaking ugly. They confuse you. Its hard to identify units unless you put your cursor over each one so it can tell you what they are. Its horrid! Also I was lead to believe the settlements were or could grow to be huge. But after several siege battles they  look nothing like the Siege of Carthage trailer portrays it to look like. Also no cut scenes for each faction before playing  to set you in the mood and not General's speeches just really saddened me. I always looked  forward to them. Options for this  game are very limited. I liked the other games more, as they gave you more options in the way you  could expand. Instead this  game gives you strict guidelines and  the diplomacy is  STILL broken. The AI ALWAYS tries to screw you and sometimes its impossible to even get trade rights (which is crazy). After conquering the British Isles I got  bored to  tears. The whole thing is  SOOOO slow. The wait time in between turns are also insanely long. Look, I own ALL the Total War  titles and I can say this  was the worst and the biggest let down. I can't say I hate it. But I wont be playing it much. Absolutely NOT WORTH THE $60 they want for it. Its corny as hell. Maybe I wouldn't be so mad if it were a $20 game. But  it  is just  not worth  the  money or hassle at the time. Check back when  a Darthmod is released. till then have fun with the other titles in the series.

title: Pretty Darn Good
text: If you  haven't played Sims in a long time or  its your first time it may take a bit to get used to this game. Make sure you only play this game when you have plenty of free time. While  you may not have a huge area to explore they do improve your options from Sims 2. You can play Arcades, use computers and such  to find jobs, chat with other sims, or go to the boardwalk and learn to play the guitar. Also having pets is a bonus if you want them, but you don't have to have  them either which is cool as I didn't really want any. You can choose where you  want to  live. You can also build and customize like all the Sims which is freaking awesome. Overall its pretty darn fun on long road trips or just relaxing in the bedroom and play. This game can be fun for all ages so long as children can read and understand financial stuff like your mortgage or rent. I really like this game even though it doesn't compare to the PC/Console versions. That said I give it a 4 star rating just because it has some shortcomings. Its not quit as fun as the Xbox or PC version, but  all that  said, sometimes I am not in the Mood to play Lego, Mario, or Pokémon games. In  those cases this game is very addictive. You can spend upward of 3 or even 4 hours playing in some cases. Hope this review helps somebody out.

title: Pros & Cons review
text:
Ok let me start by saying that this game is really fun but it does have some fatal flaws that you should look at before buying it.

The Pros:
-Good Campaign Story
-Brought Back and Revolutionized Zombies
-A lot of Extra Map Packs for Purchase
-A new and better lvling system in multiplayer
-A wide Range of Gun selection
-No more Noob-Tubing
-You can now Purchase your guns with money you earn rather than break your back with stupid achievements.
-You can Make your own Emblem
-Way better Killstreaks
-Improved Graphics
-Overall Very Fun!

The Cons:
-Campaign Gameplay is rather bland
-You'll lose connection to the game host more often
-Some Guns are not Accurately portrayed (Some Guns like M16 are 3 round bursts only and FAMAS is full auto only, also the AK47 is weaker than the M16?)
-They got rid of the SCAR

title: Buggy! Vista users Beware, will not launch game!
text: I want to say first off that this is a pretty good game. The fun factor is 9/10 for sure for me, and I beat the game 4 times. That said, I had to buy it for Xbox. The PC version is not user friendly in the least! You will be able to install your game but unable to play it on vista! I have checked around on 7 different sites, no one can give a straight answer to the problem! Even if you manage to play the game it does have a lot of glitching and freezing at some points, mostly while opening things and running around a lot. But from time to time throwing grenades can also trigger it. Don't get me wrong, the game itself is fun, customizing is average as I would have liked to choose from a variety f faces, attires, and saber styles for the get go. Choosing your path is a bit too straight forward it seems, but all and all it is a fun game. Once you have beaten it about 3 times you are ready to retire it for a LONG time. After a year or two you may go back to it again, only to realize it's shear simplicity. That said, once I was able to play the game smoothly the first few times, it was pretty epic considering when it came out and all. Comparing it to games today it still gets a fairly decent score in the fun department. I would still give it 7/10 for the fun and back then a 9/10. So why the one star? Well because I was refering more to being able to play the Xbox version, this PC version was never able to launch and so if the game can't be played how can it be any good?

title: Great MMO!
text: I've been playing early access for a day now and this game has totally blown me away.  I'm a MMO veteran and have been part of many launches, and so far I applaud Bioward and EA for doing a great job in terms of steadily allowing early access and maintaining good load on all servers.  The game runs smoothly without any crashes or issues at all so far.  To succeed, each new generation of MMOs must be able to both innovate and adopt the good elements from past games, and The Old Republic in my eyes have done both pretty well.  The innovation is mostly in the gripping story line as you level from 1-50.  You actually feel your character grow and see the reason behind doing the specific quests you are doing.  The voice acting is a la Mass Effect, good and not too drawn out.  Overall I am not disappointed at this game one bit, and I think they lived up to the hype and budget.

title: Great Workout
text:
First I would like to say that this game was a lot of fun. I got it yesterday and played it for an hour and was sweating so much it was crazy. If you're a MJ fan, then this is the perfect game for you. I danced, I sang, then I danced some more. Interesting enough it wasn't hard to follow the moves from the pictograms or even MJ himself because they depicted his signature moves. I'm totally in love with this game.

Now for the bad... unlocking training videos, really? Training and warm/up videos should have been a feature that is available to the user before they begin attempting the dance moves and not something that the user gets after he has attempted the dance moves. The next thing that I found annoying was that I had to enter my name each time I completed a song. I should have been assigned a avatar/user at the beginning of the game to eliminate this need.

Overall, BIG FUN!!! But, I couldn't in good conscience give this game the full five stars because of the problems with game usability. The realism and fun of the songs and dance moves are a solid 6 stars but the usability is a only worthy of 2 stars. Thus, I'll compromise with a rating of 4 stars.

title: Stands out from the croud
text:
I've been using this headset more or less exclusively for the past few months, from listening to/editing music and videos, to playing video games such as CS:GO, Battlefield 4 & Hardline, Arma II and III, GTA V, Skyrim, etc. During this time I've noticed what this headset is capable of, and I must say that it is amazing. I've used a multitude of comparable headsets over the years, SteelSeries, Logitechs, Turtle Beaches, Razers, pretty much anything I could get my hands on for under $200. I must say that the HyperX Cloud II's are, from my experience, among the best, not to mention among the few you can really use as normal headphones on the commute if you wanted to.

Pros:
-Lightweight
-Sturdy and visibly well crafted
-Comfortable
-Good, clean bass, for those nice explosions or just for music
-Clear highs and lows for good sound quality
-Useful features, for instance the detachable mic and inline volume/mic controls
-Useful extras included, like the nice carrying bag, extra ear cushions and extended usb cord
-Aesthetically pleasing

Cons:
-Very loud, at least compared to the Razer Kraken 7.1 Chroma's I switched from, might be my soundcard, might be that the Razers were just quiet

Conclusion: Out of all the headsets I've purchased and used over the years, these are one of the only two I'm comfortable wearing for very long periods of time, the other being the SteelSeries Siberia line, but these have better sound and mic quality and added extras to sweeten the deal. When it comes down to price, I'd have to say not many headsets are even worth a mention with these around. Well worth the money.

title: You can more or less summarize this headset with the term "Meh".
text:
I must say that before we get into the summary and brief comparisons to other headsets, that I have used a very large variety of gaming headsets and non-gaming headphones with a desk microphone. If you haven't tried out more than a couple set-ups, this may seem like a great headset, but please, trust me when I say this, you can find so much better for this price range.

Comfort:
They are plastic, obviously, which allows them to flex considerably, but it feels rather cheap so I wouldn't do anything crazy. They do indeed fit, and I have a very large head, however the ear cups are horrid and hurt quite a bit because no matter how I put them on they still don't cover the back of my ear, resting on top of my ears. They are intended to go over, and I by no means have large ears, but for me they do not house my ears like say Steel Series Siberia V2's, Logitech G430's, Plantronics GameCom 780's or HyperX Cloud II's do by experience. Overall I would give it a 3/10 in comfort.

Sound & Microphone:
The sound quality is also okay, the highs are pretty clear, but the lows are very muffled and the bass is almost non-existent. As far as Surround Sound goes, that part is definitely true, and very noticeable in any FPS. Now to the mic, it legitimately sounds worse than $10 desktop mics you can buy on Amazon. It is muffled, sounds very distant even when placed half an inch from your face. Now that I've bashed it almost as much as it deserves, there is a slight positive to the microphone in that it will not pick up anything that is further than 4 inches away from it, unless you fire a gun or something, even then you will probably have to be within a foot for it to pick that up. I'm not sure if this is the same with all of them, or if it is this one in particular, but I've tested it for a little over an hour tweaking every setting with third party as well as Gamdias's own software, and I have to speak up considerably for it to pick me up well enough to make a video. As far as sound quality goes, I will give it a 6/10, whereas microphone quality gets a solid 2/10.

Build Quality:
After a few weeks of using these for a few hours a day, I've come to the conclusion that these are incredibly poorly made. I know that is more or less obvious upon picking them up and moving them around, but sometimes things can surprise you when it comes to how sturdy they are regardless of how they initially feel. When you try to put these on, you feel like they are going to snap right where the metal arcs connect to the plastic. Whenever you re-adjust because the ear cups are starting to hurt, the connection between the ear cups and the body of the headphones creaks, unnaturally so. A few other pairs of headphones I've had also do this, but not nearly to the extent where it worries you. The wire is pretty well made, wrapped in nylon instead of a cheap rubber, and doesn't feel like it will fall apart or unwind easily. The little remote that extends your auxiliary cable and converts it to USB seems sturdy enough, even though it too has a cheap brittle plastic feel to it. All things said and done I think it deserves a 6/10 for build quality, as it has yet to fall apart.

With all of that said, I would definitely not suggest this as a purchase, you will more than likely be much happier with almost anything else you can find in this price range, such as a SteelSeries Siberia V2 headset (Currently also $49.99).

title: Works as expected, nicely made
text:
This is a good value product made well that does just what you want it to do.
The construction seems high quality--cable is braided, well made, flexible. Time will tell, but I don't anticipate any issues
The controller works fine plugged in. The cord is a little shy of 10 feet and don't forget you'll want some slack when you figure out if that's long enough. Any shorter and I think most people wouldn't find it useful for playing while charging. it could be longer, but 10 feet seems like a moderate length.
The battery for me fit in quite tightly, so much so at first that I was a little worried. I'm always hesitant when things need some force. But it does click into place without issue; just as noted definitely tight.
I haven't tested the 25 hour claim, but it's lasted multiple days of multiple hours of play, certainly into the teens.

Amazon Basics have been mostly great values so far that I've experienced and this seems no different
