title: Great for Watching Special Effects Movies, Overall Excellent But Pricey
text:
Here's my review for what it's worth:

First, I'm a movie and music buff, not a gamer, and I usually prefer earbuds rather than headphones for my Samsung Galaxy 4S Blaze. I typically prefer lightweight, easy to pack headphones when I travel and am a little mystified about why there's been a throwback to much bulkier versions, like the ones from the 60s and 70s. Maybe I'm just getting old, but I don't see how bulk is better.

That said, I have to say I felt very cool wearing these red and black headphones. They are almost a dead ringer for the trendy Dr. Dre Beats headphones lots of kids wear these days. However, upon closer inspection, I can see these are so much better made, with small details that really make a difference in comfort and function.

PROS: Overall solidly made, though the plastic parts make me wonder how much use it will take before those vulnerable parts break. Judging by the other reviews I've read of this product, I have reason to be concerned.

Sound quality is excellent. I watched "Titanic" and "The Impossible" on my Windows PC and the surround sound was fantastic. I'm reserving these headphones for movie nights when disaster films are on my agenda.

Music. You can adjust the timbre, bass, etc., using the Bluetooth app. While I'm not a professional musician and there are those of us out there who are more discerning, I was quite impressed with the depth and clarity of the jazz, classical and rock tunes I tested these with. Bass started to crap out at a very high volume, but I would rarely use it at that extreme.

Comfortable to wear and lightweight, despite the size. Your head feels less sore because of a cushion cleverly stitched on the underside of the band that rests on top of your head. I can see myself using this on an airplane for hours, and the manufacturer encourages this by providing an adapter for flight use. Clever.

Easy to fold and store. Again, I'm not a fan of big headphones, so I'm glad I can shrink them down whichever way I can. I do wish, however, that the manufacturer had made the headpiece bendable and foldable as well, not just the muffs. For $300 why not?

Versatile. I like the fact it can be used like an ordinary headphone with a cord, used wirelessly for your cell and once charged, pumped up with surround sound for movie watching. Whatever situation you want, these headphones offer it. It comes with Bluetooth, USB, and 3.5mm jack cords.

The buttons are conveniently placed, though all of them are located on the right earmuff - if you're a lefty you'd have to switch. I especially loved the fact that I can control the volume by simply reaching up to the headphone and rolling the dial.

CONS: The included USB cable is kind of thick, which is good for durability, but it's also kind of short. I would have liked it to be longer.

The storage case has a zipper on the back, making you assume the cords would be naturally stored there. But the compartment is tight and stiff, and it makes the package bulky. I ended up wrapping the cord up with a pipe cleaner and putting it inside with the headphones. Not sure what I would use the exterior zipper compartment for.

Noise cancellation. The noise cancellation was OK but not as impressive as the BOSE headphones I used to own. I feel as if the noise cancellation works mainly because the earpiece covers the entire ear rather than having a true noise cancellation mechanism.

I still have to test these using SKYPE, but for now I'm impressed with these. For $300, I would not expect anything less.

title: it's pretty..but thats all.
text:
UPDATE 4-------
OK. now the eye candy has completely worn off. And I can see clearly, for the first time, that this game is just NOT a good 'simcity' at all. The cities are so small. And even such, I could live with 'probably', but even with the small cities, they limit the tools you have to work with. They only let you put a little bit of bus stations, street car depos, and NO subway. Even a small city needs more than they let you have. These people are banking on the fact that you will be overcome with the 'pretty' aspect of the game, and not notice how limiting it is. My nephew has a PS3 and the graphics, on this game, are about on par with his system. Graphics are no big deal anymore. Sorry Origin.
UPDATE 3-------
Twice, tonight. The system crashed. I just wanted to nix the schools in my ONE city, as so they would send their population over to city Two's way. And maybe they could make their city an educational one, for a specialaztion. But two, I was shut down. So now, they lose another star, from me. Although this is a PRETTY, PRETTY, eye candy game. It's, simulation quality, was not an aspect they cared much about. The MAIN work was put into the cosmetics of the game. Not the realism, part.

UPDATE 2-------
OK. They lose another star from me. For 3 days now, and this is the third, so it COULD continue tomorrow. The program has crashed on start up. Requiring a shutdown of the program, and reload all the way back to where you were, usually about 5 minutes. I really thought that the Sim-city was OVER the crashes. If you do get this, don't have, very high exceptions for it. Just the eye candy part. It is ABSOLUTELY BEAUTIFUL. But beauty is only special until the NEWNESS wears down.
UPDATE-------
as of may 14-2013, the hosting company 'Origin' has brought some more servers online to handle the increased bandwidth needed for all the Sim City players. And also, after the initial release, there has not been so GREAT of a demand on the servers. So the WAITING for a place in line to get a server, is almost over. There is still the occasional hiccup in the system, so it only gets a 4 star so far.

good points.
The game 'Sim city' has always been extremely error ridden. In every version, since the beginning back in the 1990's. I played this on my Amiga 2000. I thought it was awesome, but it crashed when my city got to a big size. And so did all the subsequent editions. Except for this one. They keep on 'patching' the program, as problems are discovered. And they are adhering to the job, rather well. I've reduced my action on the game to 2 times a week. But 1 of those times, will install a new update package, 3 minutes total. So on, that front, I am very pleased.

The graphics. Absolutely breathtaking. I think this must be the entire defination of the term 'eye candy'. I bet it takes all the power I have, an i7 3.4Ghz, 16 G ram, but there is NO slowdown or any other adverse effects. Well written code.

In conclusion.
Yes, I would buy the program again now. They were NOT ready to ship this on opening day, but the weather is better now. There is still an issue sometimes with getting a server. But if you have time to take an hour out, it'll be OK. Now, if you made a date to do this, with a Lil' time window, that has no room for alteration. That would not work. But I don't have those criteria. 'I' like the program, too much, to 'not' play it. so YES, I would buy the program.

I cannot even play the game, because of busy servers. I've been trying every 6 hours, for the last 36 hours. No server, then there was a server, it said. But after a big dance around and around, it could not connect to the server. I don't think there ever was a server. Shame on you, Maxis.

title: Possibly the best of it's kind.
text:
I hate to sound like a fanboy, but the Razer Naga is the best MMO gaming mouse I've tried. I've tried alot of mice.

This will be my second Naga. My previous one wore out after over 5 years of using it more than I should have. It's only that the button under the scroll wheel wore out. I'm surprised that any mouse lasted as long as the Naga did.

The buttons take some getting used to. It took me about a year to consistently use all of the side buttons. The last row always felt kind of awkward to reach. Those are buttons I rarely use anyways.

One thing I noticed about this particular model of Naga is that my previous one had a switch that changed between the keyboard numbers and the number pad. This one has no switch and only functions off the keyboard numbers.

The mouse is a good size and the buttons are responsive. My biggest gripe with other gaming mice are that they are often oddly shaped or way too large, and are made of cheap materials.

title: This game is a blast...
text:
I'm not a Star Wars fan, but this game is so much fun. I haven't had this much fun on a game for a long time.

GOOD:

There are so many vehicles to use. There are also some cool characters....and jetpacks. The levels are creative and the "capture the base" style play keeps respawn play strategic. Playing with so many bots gives a big battle feel that I haven't experienced in a game. Also, there are many details from the SW movies that are added into the levels.

BAD:

The online servers aren't set up very well. It's hard to find a game with a friend, or any specific room at all. Also, some of the blaster guns trail way behind your crosshairs and this gets annoying. As with any online shooter there are occasional teamkillers.

If you like first person shooters and/or Star Wars than get this game. It seems that Lucas Arts is releasing online patches quite often to fix all the problems in this game.

text:
For anyone that has played the first Socom game, don't expect "Socom 1 with new maps." This game has quite a few changes.

Good:

There are still rarely ever any online cheaters. The game is lots of fun and is probably the best online shooter for PS2.

BAD:

There are a lot of bugs in the game. Hit detection and lag are really bad, so it is common for your shots not to register. Also, the weapons are inbalanced and not consistant.

I have gotten my moneys worth on this game. It is now a greatest hit and only $20.00 new....I would pay that just for the offline portion!!!

If you like this type of game I would also recommend Star Wars Battlefronts.

title: Great VR device, overall better.
text:
The Oculus Rift S has the right idea with the inside out tracking. Having to setup various sensors (like on the previous rift) was a pain, but worked well enough. The problem was the amount of USB ports it consumed, as well as running many cords throughout the room. So far some of the games don't work as well, but when I mess with certain games they run as smooth as can be. I beleive with a few patches this will be perfect, since it just seems that the problems are minor, and can be tuned through software updates.

some Pros:
-Much clearer visuals. I can read signs in game, and everything looks much more clear.
-Better head-strap. Easy to readjust when someone else wants to try it. Not much explaining.
-Portabliity. I can easily take this to a friends place without having to take and resetup the sensors.

some cons:
-some games aren't adjusted right just yet (although all VR headsets had problems initially).
-Great audio gone. Apparently they will try and remedy this with an update, but you can use your own headphones.
I've read that many don't fit on it, so do your research before you buy a pair.
-Display port connector. You must have a display port to make this work. You can get an adapter, but I have not tried this.
-IPD problems. I have not had any myself, but people that have eyes more widely spread apart (the distance between pupils)
should make sure that they can use this without issue.

title: what a disappointment
text:
The TLDR version:

I am giving the game 2 stars because it is fun at first, but if I could give the endgame a negative rating for being a cynical mechanism for extracting the maximum amount of money and/or time from players in return for unpleasant and unrewarding gameplay, I would.

The details:
I played both D1 and D2, and while I have fond memories of them, I don't feel all that attached to the franchise. Nonetheless I was looking forward to it since Blizz announced its release and ponied up for the CE.

I was not one of the people who raged at release because of server crashes, glitches, bugs and frequent "maintenance" sessions lasting hours, sometimes with little or no warning. I figured that Blizz was fielding a lot of new ideas and processes with this game. I was happy with the game, despite huge numbers of reports of botting, duping, hacking, exploits, session spoofing, etc, I figured it didn't really affect me or the people I played with. I was wrong about that, but never mind.

Then two things happened: the Real Money Auction House (RMAH) and patch 1.3. I think others have probably gone into a lot of detail about why those two things proved real game changers for more casual players like myself, but for me the net change was that the "end game", such as it is, is now basically pay to win. You need not only to play skillfully, and to understand your class inside and out, which I would expect, but in addition you need really really good gear. Gear that, because of the way itemization works in the game, you will not get by farming. You must go to the AH, where you will need millions, yes millions, of gold per end game item (unless you want to spend hours surfing the terrible, horrid AH interface for the occasional deal). A little to much for ya? Well, off you go to the RMAH, where you can buy what you need for real money! Don't worry, there's a per-item cap of $250, so you can't go overboard.

Subsequent patches have only reduced the options of making in-game gold legitimately, and many of the changes seem to force players more and more to the RMAH as Blizz figures out where exactly players are managing to farm gold and items, and then nerfs those places one after the other.

Knowing what I know now, would I buy this game again? No, and for sure not the Collector's edition. The one nice thing I can say about the CE is that it did include a free copy of D2, which has been fun to check out again since I stopped playing D3...

Should you buy this game.? Maybe... I had fun with it through Hell Difficulty and Act 1 Inferno before the RMAH/patch 1.3/repair cost fiasco. If you feel that playing up through Hell Difficulty will give you $60 bucks worth of satisfaction, then it might be worth it. PersonalIy, I was hoping for a little more longevity, but oh well. *Goes off to play Path of Exile*

title: Great old skhool games
text:
The games on this cartridge are very old school. The basic premise of each game is very simple, but mastering the game is difficult. On Runner, for example, you must make it through the each entire several minute level without any errors or you are immediately whisked back to the start. For some reason, I never found myself really getting too frustrated by this even though I would at times have to replay a level a hundred times before I got all the way through. The music, with its chip tunes and consistent beats, allows the player to zone out while playing.

The games all work well on the 3ds--easy to pick up and play, but deep enough to stick with for hours.

Cost
In line amp (for non pc users)
Wire length
multiplatform headset

Comfort
Construction
Build quality

title: Don't let the non-Sony official status scare you
text:
I was hesitant to order this charging station since it isn't an official Sony product, but I also was getting tired of having to sit three feet in front of my TV so I could play video games with the controller plugged in to charge.

I'm glad I got over my reluctance and ordered this product. I pop the controller into the dock when I'm done gaming for the night and my controller is charged when I go to the play the next day, leaving my USB ports open to charge my headset (which has reached the end of its battery life).

My only complaint (and this is a controller design, not the charging station) is that when the controller is charging it emits a yellow light that cycles between dim to bright. Because the controllers are charged with the light bar facing the ceiling, the light can get pretty bright if your room is dark.

title: Lovely typing experience! Worriesome USB port.
text:
Just got this keyboard today. It makes me wonder why I didn't get a mechanical keyboard earlier! Perfectly surmises what I was missing in keyboards over the last 10 or so years.

I got the brown switches, and the noise level is just right, and will probably get better when I learn to stop typing so heavily!

Build quality is impressive. Has a nice heft. LEDS for the "lock" lights are blue, and there is a subtle red background behind the keys.

My one concern, and the one voiced by many other reviewers, is for the removable wire and the USB connection. It comes out at a right angle, so if your cord needs to run right, it has to make a U-turn as the plug outputs the cable to the left. This could be replaced with a standard USB cable though I think.

My current plan is to hot glue the cable to the back of the keyboard, with the hopes of adding a new stress point for when the cable gets invariably bumped or tugged at.

title: PUNCHES PULLED!
text:
too many punches pulled by Capcom with this offering.

Been a Capcom faithfull since forever ago, like 20 something years. That said, I have bought and continue to buy pretty much any and every SF product.

SFxT is not good. Its tough to say that. Why? The single player is cool and works well, graphics are great, the backgrounds are very interactive and awesome. The problems arise in creating button/controller schemes, the gem system, DLC, and last but not least, the AWFUL ONLINE EXPERIENCE.

How Capcom could knowlingly release this with online play the way it is is remarkable. Literally, NO SOUND. Can't play a game where HADOKEN is as synanamous with graphics and playability. This alone renders this game defective. I know many games playable online are not perfect, but usually, its due to connection issues. Here however, Capcom's "tradeoff" was sound for playability. Not cool and thats a no go for me. Also, the quick combo chains are a joke to any real player and make this game much to easy, the lack of available buttons if not using a PS3 controller; this game is balance & tradeoff and fails compared to how solid SF4 is.

Otherwise, if you are into an overly styalized faster paced fighting game, this one is up there. The wheels fall off online, and in the end, if you are a true SF player, all that matters is the fight between you and the other guy, which is just not enjoyable here.

title: high learning curve high reward
text:
UPDATE: since the arrival of Grand Slam Tennis 2 - Top Spin 4 has elevated to the top even more so. What GST2 makes you realize is just how accurate and nuanced TS4 is. If you are trying to decide what tennis game is for you, look no further than TS4, especially if you are a tennis player. The game is captured ALMOST perfectly, lovely courts, sounds, details, etc, and for those looking for a REWARDING game, TS4 has a steep learning curve that only makes the game better with time and age well. Still the best choice. And lets face it, if a tennis video game had you hitting errors that reflect real life, NO ONE would play the game, so keeping the ball generally in versus out is favorable. TS4 has a nice balance, if you are late on your backswing, late to a ball, hit a harder "get" etc, it will be an error or a BAD shot resulting in the opponent hitting a winner. Pretty much, TS4 keeps the tennis going when you cant get on a real court. And, you wont see any player hitting make believe shots like Nadal w/1 handed topspin backhand, or playing Serve/Volley like a master, or fake tennis shots etc. Stick to TS4.

best tennis game out. hands down. problem is, the game ships with a crap instruction book and many elements of the game you will have to discover and uncover as you hit as many balls as possible. the game does not come out and tell you that, for instance, you can use the buttons for a power serve, yet if you serve by buttons, the speed of the balls will be on average about 10-30 mph SLOWER (depending on timing) than if you use the right stick. Another instance is returning...timing a button press or holding down for power? What to do? The mechanics remain a little unclear as well...how do you really hit a control shot, what is the timing of any shot, how do you hit a great drop shot? Any and all of this is really force fed by hitting as many balls as possible in all situations and figuring it out. Simply put, the "controls" are only the starting point to know how to really play this game.

That said, once you play enough balls, this the closest thing to real tennis. Players look, feel, swing as authentic as they are in real life. Sometimes during game play, i feel as though im watching my favorite tennis players play a match. Most of the players are well balanced, there are a few that seem to really be the best in the game no matter how you play them, but overall...pretty good balance across the board. Pure fact is that nadal will get just about every ball on the court and roddicks serve is sometimes unbeatable depending on the level of skill of the player. But, true in real life as well sometimes.

Areas of improvement...wish the serve/return game was a little more solid, also wish playing a tough shot was a little harder, although the risk/reward is pretty good, many shots that would cause errors do not. But some patches to the game made things better. it should be a little easier to hit winners, sometimes I feel as though im playing virtua tennis again, but thankfully at least TS actually lets you hit winners, but there should be more of them.

title: Not bad
text:
I bought this for purposes other than playing fighting games (but do use it for fighting games)

Briefly
1. the stick itself is not tall enough; from the base to the ball its like an inch and a half. For people who like to use the palm of their hand instead, this may be hard, especially with bigger hands
2. the top part rotates; not sure if this is a positive or negative quality, but when i move the joystick sometimes i just rotate the top while not moving the stick, theres no friction from the ball on the metal post
3. The base should be bigger so you can rest at least some of your hands in front of the buttons and next to the joystick

Other than that, for 45bucks...this is pretty hard to beat, the quality is very good, inputs are accurate, the buttons are not flimsy...cant beat this stick at its price...its just a less expensive alternative to the 100+ ones -- drawback is its size...great stick on a budget

title: Competition
text:
Wii sports was a good showcase of the system. Resort takes that, flips it on its head, and gets you to have FUN with so much more control integration...but....there is an added level of competition here that is defiant throughout your resort vacation. Every game, imo, gets very, very competitive in a way that wii sports 1 never reached due to the basic who can waggle better (?). Prepare to sweat, prepare your curse words, prepare to be very angry at your oppenents!! Instead of listing what is bad and good, ill just list the games that are more or less ehhh

Fencing seems great at first, and you are wowed by the coolness, however, after many matches against people of all skill levels - this game is NOT waggle-proof. The hardest wagglers (like my gf) will win almost all the time, no matter what skill level you are. A straight waggle fest dominates this game, which is a bit dissapointing. There is a defensive counter attack, but a very hard determined waggler can break through it!

Wave Running - in theory cool, but keeping the boat going straight is an issue

Canoeing - Cool, again, getting the boat on your intended course is difficult, when you switch sides to steer, sometimes the game does not recognize it, but wow WHAT A WORK OUT

The rest of the games...are...AWESOME. The graphical presentation is up 10 fold, the subtle music is cool and not annoying, but the best are the signature Nintendo'd sound effects that make every game addicting and unique.

I will conclude and say this is a MUST BUY by any means, whether you play alone or with friends, this game is so much fun, and highly competitive, with 2+ player modes abound, and different variations (playing against eachother, or, playing collectively, unlocking bonus modes/activities) For [...] bucks, cant beat it, and its a must have, with almost perfect controls in every game, a few games are a little lackluster, but still fun.

Wii Sports Resort has made Wii Sports 1 into a game of SKILL, and your abilities in the game will be tested against your oppenents which makes for one heck of a competitive fun fest. Pure Nintendo, pure fun, and you will be sweating!!

title: not for casual wii-ers
text:
UPDATE 2 - after about 20 hrs of play, I will flat out say this is the best, by far, tennis/gaming experience i've ever been able to play. The depth of control with Wii Motion is unreal. Invest the time, and you will be SMILING ear to ear playing this, and then probably wanting to go take some tennis lessons too. EA gets a knod, I have not been a fan of them for quite some time, but everything in this game is done right to MAKE THE GAME FUN...awesome, awesome. You feel the adreneline flow before tryingto return a HUGE Sampras serve, knowing hes coming into net - the look and feel of EACH pro is just like real life (even given the graphics of this game) you feel the mounting pressure of a cross court rally, the crowd erupts, your playe reacts - what a game.

Well...the wiimotion plus is out, and so are 2 tennis games.

Ive been playing tennis my entire life, and can tell you that if you are a waggle-er from wii sports, you may just want to stick to it. GST is no joke, requires real, fluid,controlled swings, competent play, and constant attention to the wii mote/your hand. This is not demanding, its real - you would not be able to hit a tennis ball if you kept the racket hanging by your side until it was time to swing - getting the racket back before the ball needs to be hit, preparation for your swing, all the things needed for real tennis are in this game. You will have to prepare your shots, be set up, and take a real back swing - or else, you will wind up like other gamers out there complaining that controls are off, what you (think) you are doing is not coming out on screen.

Get ready to invest serios time into learning this game, but the benefits are great, and the rallies are awesome. Dont be swayed by the cartoon graphics...this game is the first game I have played that actually captures real tennis, the sounds of the court, the serious voice of the announcers, it has a very very authentic feel, powerful racket contact sounds, and its very real compared to the artificial nature of virtua tennis - virtua tennis 3 was so robotic it was horrendous to play, and if you are a tennis player, virtua tennis is much too arcade ish to really feel a reward if and when you put a ball down the line for a winner.

In virtua tennis - there is not such thing as hitting a ball OUT. in GST, you bet you can hit it out, go for too much - you will be dissapointed when you hit it 1 ft off the sideline. the game rewards you with good play, smart shot selection, and execution whereas in VT - the game wants the ball in play and you can do no wrong.

Being able to slice, lob, DROP, top spin etc, all in real time, and for the most part putting the ball where you want, its just awesome.

spend AT LEAST an hr with the ball machine - u know you have mastered the controls when you say "i want it cross ct" and you put it cross ct, i want a inside out forehand, and you do it, every time. then its time to play - just like real tennis.

UPDATE - MOST IMPORTANT THING - MAKE SURE THAT INBETWEEN POINTS YOU KEEP THE WIIMOTE LEVEL AND POINTED AT THE SCREEN AND STEADY - EVERY POINT YOU WILL HAVE A PERFECT CALIBRATED DEAD CENTER RACKET - THIS MAKES ALL THE DIFFERENCE IN THE WORLD.

This is not demanding, its real - you would not be able to hit a tennis ball if you kept the racket hanging by your side until it was time to swing - getting the racket back before the ball needs to be hit, preparation for your swing, all the things needed for real tennis are in this game. You will have to prepare your shots, be set up, and take a real back swing - or else, you will wind up like other gamers out there complaining that controls are off, what you think you are doing is not coming out on screen. Get ready to invest serios time into learning this game, but the benefits are great, and the rallies are awesome. Dont be swayed by the cartoon graphics...this game is the first game I have played that actually captures real tennis, the sounds of the court, the serious voice of the announcers, it has a very very authentic feel, powerful racket contact sounds, and its very real compared to the artificial nature of virtua tennis - virtua tennis 3 was so robotic it was horrendous to play, and if you are a tennis player, virtua tennis is much too arcade ish to really feel a reward if and when you put a ball down the line for a winner. In virtua tennis - there is not such thing as hitting a ball OUT. in GST, you bet you can hit it out, go for too much - you will be dissapointed when you hit it 1 ft off the sideline. the game rewards you with good play, smart shot selection, and execution whereas in VT - the game wants the ball in play and you can do no wrong. Being able to slice, lob, DROP, top spin etc, all in real time, and for the most part putting the ball where you want, its just awesome. spend AT LEAST an hr with the ball machine - u know you have mastered the controls when you say "i want it cross ct" and you put it cross ct, i want a inside out forehand, and you do it, every time. then its time to play - just like real tennis. UPDATE - MOST IMPORTANT THING - MAKE SURE THAT INBETWEEN POINTS YOU KEEP THE WIIMOTE LEVEL AND POINTED AT THE SCREEN AND STEADY - EVERY POINT YOU WILL HAVE A PERFECT CALIBRATED DEAD CENTER RACKET - THIS MAKES ALL THE DIFFERENCE IN THE WORLD.
